steps.instructions: Observe how the device reports battery status. Action: Power on the BladderScan BVI 9400 and check the battery icon or charge indication. Place the device on the charger and observe whether the battery status changes. Allow the unit to remain on charge long enough to determine whether charge level increases. Expected outcome: Battery status should show charging and gradually improve. If the charge level never changes despite verified charger power and proper docking, suspect battery, dock, charging circuit, or internal power issue.

steps.title: 8. Compare With a Known-Good Charger or Dock if Available
steps.instructions: This helps separate scanner failure from charging accessory failure. Action: Place the scanner on a known-good compatible charger or dock if one is available. Alternatively, test a known-good BVI 9400 on the suspect charger if your facility has another compatible unit. Expected outcome: If the problem follows the scanner, suspect battery or internal scanner issue. If the problem stays with the charger or dock, suspect charger, dock, or power supply issue. If a faulty charger is confirmed, remove the charger from service and replace or repair it according to facility process.

steps.title: 9. Check for Battery Age or Usage Pattern
steps.instructions: Poor runtime may be caused by an aging battery rather than an immediate charging failure. Action: Review service history, battery replacement history, and staff reports. Look for patterns such as: Device charges fully but dies quickly. Runtime is poor after normal charging. Battery percentage drops suddenly. Scanner powers off during scan activity. Battery has not been replaced in several years. Expected outcome: Battery condition is assessed based on age, symptoms, and history. If the battery is aged or runtime remains poor after normal charging, remove the scanner from service for battery evaluation or replacement.

steps.title: 10. Perform a Controlled Runtime Check if Safe
steps.instructions: Do this only off-patient and only if it does not delay clinical care. Action: Fully charge the device using a verified charger. Power the device on and monitor whether the battery drains unusually fast during normal standby or test use. Do not use the device clinically during this evaluation if reliability is questionable. Expected outcome: Runtime should be reasonable and stable. If runtime drops quickly or the device shuts off unexpectedly, remove the device from service.

steps.title: 11. Inspect for Heat, Swelling, Odor, or Damage
steps.instructions: Battery-related problems can become safety issues. Action: Check the scanner and charging base for: Unusual heat. Burning smell. Cracked housing. Swollen battery area. Discoloration near charging contacts. Intermittent power when moved. Signs of liquid damage. Expected outcome: No unsafe physical condition is present. If heat, odor, swelling, liquid damage, or physical damage is found, stop troubleshooting immediately, remove the device from service, label it Out of Service, and escalate for repair.

steps.title: 12. Verify Final Device Status
steps.instructions: Before returning the scanner to service, confirm reliable operation. Action: Confirm the scanner powers on normally. Confirm charging indicator behavior is normal. Confirm the device holds charge long enough for expected clinical use. Confirm no power interruptions occur during handling or scanning setup. Expected outcome: The BladderScan BVI 9400 charges properly and operates reliably. If confirmed, return the device to service and document the work order.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Verathon BladderScan BVI 9400 would not hold a charge and powered off shortly after being removed from the charging dock.
CCR.Cause: Verified outlet and charger power were good, charging contacts were clean, and the scanner still showed poor runtime after a full charge.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the BladderScan BVI 9400 from service, labeled it Out of Service, and sent it for battery and charging system evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Charging dock or power supply tested
Any unusual heat, odor, swelling, or damage
Whether issue followed scanner or charger
Final device status: returned to service or removed from service

title: Verathon BladderScan BVI 9400 Bladder Scanner - Printer or results documentation failure
description: Troubleshooting failed printouts, missing scan results, poor print quality, or documentation problems after bladder volume measurement.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not delay patient care while troubleshooting a documentation issue. Remove the BladderScan BVI 9400 from patient use if scan results cannot be reliably displayed, printed, or documented. If the scanner is needed for active patient care, use another approved bladder scanner or follow the facility’s alternate assessment process. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without relying on incomplete or missing documentation. Why it matters: A bladder scanner may still scan correctly, but missing or incorrect documentation can affect clinical decisions and charting accuracy. If this resolves the immediate clinical need, stop and document the issue.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Documentation Failure
steps.instructions: Confirm exactly what is failing before assuming a printer problem. Ask clinical staff what occurred: No printout produced; Printout is blank; Printout is faded or unreadable; Wrong or missing patient/result information; Results do not save; Scan result disappears before documentation; Staff cannot transfer or record results. Perform a test scan or review a recent stored result if available. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to printing, result storage, user workflow, or scanner function. Why it matters: “Printer not working” may actually be a paper issue, battery issue, user workflow issue, or failed scan documentation process.

steps.title: Confirm the Scan Result Is Actually Available
steps.instructions: Verify that the device produced a valid bladder volume result. Power on the unit and check whether scan results appear normally on the display. Confirm that the scan completed and did not show a low-confidence result, error, or canceled scan. Expected outcome: A valid scan result is visible and available for printing or documentation. If no valid result exists, troubleshoot the scan quality or probe issue first and stop.

steps.title: Check Battery Charge and Power Status
steps.instructions: Low battery or unstable power can interfere with printing or result handling. Check the battery level indicator. Place the scanner on its charging cradle or connect it to approved power if applicable. Allow the unit to charge if the battery is low. Attempt printing again after confirming stable power. Expected outcome: The unit has enough power to complete scan documentation and printer operation. If the printer works after charging, return the device to service after confirming normal operation.

steps.title: Inspect Printer Paper Installation
steps.instructions: Check the most common external cause first. Open the printer paper compartment. Confirm that paper is present. Verify that the paper roll is installed in the correct direction for thermal printing. Make sure the paper feeds freely and is not jammed, folded, wrinkled, or misrouted. Expected outcome: Paper is loaded correctly and can advance normally. If correcting the paper roll restores printing, stop and document the resolution.

steps.title: Check for Paper Jam or Debris
steps.instructions: A small paper obstruction can prevent printing or cause partial printouts. Inspect the paper path. Remove any torn paper pieces or loose debris. Do not use sharp tools that could damage the printer mechanism. Close the paper compartment securely and attempt another print. Expected outcome: Paper feeds smoothly without binding. If the jam is cleared and printouts are normal, return the unit to service.

steps.title: Verify Thermal Paper Condition
steps.instructions: Blank or faded printouts may be caused by incorrect or degraded paper. Confirm that approved thermal paper is being used. Check if the paper appears old, glossy on the wrong side, heat damaged, or stored improperly. Replace the roll with known-good thermal paper. Attempt another print. Expected outcome: Printout becomes readable with proper thermal paper. If print quality improves, document the paper replacement and return the device to service.

steps.title: Check Printer Door or Cover Closure
steps.instructions: The printer may not operate if the cover is not fully latched. Open and reseat the printer cover. Confirm that the cover clicks or seats fully closed. Attempt to print again. Expected outcome: The printer recognizes the paper compartment as closed and prints normally. If reseating the cover resolves the issue, stop and document the finding.

steps.title: Confirm Staff Printing Workflow
steps.instructions: Make sure the failure is not caused by a missed menu step or timing issue. Review how staff are attempting to print or document the result. Confirm that the result screen is active and that the print option is selected correctly. Check whether staff are clearing, rescanning, or powering off the unit before documentation is completed. Expected outcome: The scanner is being used in the correct sequence for result documentation. If workflow correction resolves the problem, provide user guidance and document the education given.

steps.title: Check Date, Time, and Result Information
steps.instructions: Documentation may be considered failed if printouts are missing correct identifiers or timestamps. Check whether date and time appear correct on printed or displayed results. Verify whether patient ID entry, if used at the facility, is being entered correctly. Confirm that the device settings match facility expectations for result documentation. Expected outcome: Printed results contain usable scan information for clinical documentation. If settings or workflow correction resolves the issue, document what was corrected.

steps.title: Power Cycle and Retest
steps.instructions: A temporary software or printer communication issue may clear with a controlled restart. Power the BladderScan BVI 9400 off. Wait briefly. Power the unit back on. Perform or retrieve a test result and attempt printing again. Expected outcome: The printer and result documentation function normally after restart. If normal operation returns, monitor for recurrence and document the successful retest.

steps.title: Inspect for Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Printer or documentation failures may follow drops, fluid exposure, or rough handling. Inspect the scanner housing, printer cover, paper door, keypad/buttons, display, charging contacts, and probe connection. Look for: Cracked housing; Loose printer door; Missing latch; Signs of fluid ingress; Unusual smell; Heat damage; Evidence of impact. Expected outcome: No visible damage is present that would explain printer or system malfunction. If damage is found, remove the device from service and send it for repair evaluation.

steps.title: Test With Known-Good Consumables and Accessories
steps.instructions: Rule out simple external causes before escalating. Install a known-good paper roll. Confirm the device has adequate battery charge. Use the correct scanner, cradle, and accessories assigned to the unit. Attempt another print or documentation test. Expected outcome: The device prints or documents correctly with known-good external items. If the issue remains after known-good paper and power are verified, escalation is appropriate.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Verathon BladderScan BVI 9400 would scan but would not print the bladder volume result.
CCR.Cause: Troubleshooting found the thermal paper roll was installed backward, causing blank printouts.
CCR.Resolution: Reinstalled the paper roll correctly, performed a test scan printout, verified readable results, and returned the scanner to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the scan result displayed normally
Whether the issue was no print, blank print, faded print, or missing documentation
Whether known-good thermal paper was tested
Any paper jam or debris found
Whether date/time and result information printed correctly
Any visible damage, fluid exposure, heat, or unusual smell

title: Verathon BladderScan BVI 9400 Bladder Scanner - Calibration, self-test, or startup failure
description: Troubleshooting BladderScan BVI 9400 startup, self-test, or calibration problems caused by power, probe, battery, cradle, or user-accessible setup issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot the BladderScan BVI 9400 while it is being used for active patient assessment. Remove the scanner from patient use if it will not start, fails self-test, displays calibration-related errors, or gives unreliable scan behavior. Use another bladder scanner or approved clinical assessment method if bladder volume measurement is needed. Expected outcome: Patient care is not delayed or based on an unreliable device. Why it matters: A bladder scanner that fails startup, self-test, or calibration checks may produce inaccurate or unavailable measurements.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Failure
steps.instructions: Confirm exactly what the device is doing before assuming a hardware failure. Power the unit on and observe the startup sequence. Check whether the issue is unit will not power on. Check whether the issue is startup freezes. Check whether the issue is self-test fails. Check whether the issue is calibration message appears. Check whether the issue is probe is not recognized. Check whether the issue is screen is blank or dim. Check whether the issue is device powers off unexpectedly. Check whether the issue is error returns after restart. Expected outcome: The failure mode is clearly identified and documented. If the unit starts normally after restart and passes checks, return it to service only after confirming normal scan operation.

steps.title: Check Battery Charge and Battery Seating
steps.instructions: Low or unstable battery power can cause startup and self-test problems. Confirm the battery is properly installed and seated. Place the unit on the charging base or connect it to the approved charging setup. Allow the battery to charge if the charge level is low. Check for charging indicators on the unit or charger. Expected outcome: The unit powers on normally and completes startup with adequate battery power. If the issue resolves after charging or reseating the battery, document the finding and stop.

steps.title: Inspect the Charging Base and Power Supply
steps.instructions: A charging or power issue may appear as a scanner failure. Verify the charger is plugged into a known-good outlet. Inspect the power adapter, cord, and charger contacts for damage, looseness, bent pins, fluid residue, or corrosion. Test the outlet with another device or outlet tester if appropriate. If available, try a known-good compatible charger or charging base. Expected outcome: The scanner charges consistently and powers on normally. If the unit only fails with one charger or outlet, remove the faulty accessory from service.

steps.title: Inspect the Probe and Cable Connection
steps.instructions: The BVI 9400 depends on the probe and cable connection for proper startup and functional checks. Inspect the probe, cable, connector, and strain relief for visible damage. Look for bent pins, cracked housings, dried gel, fluid intrusion, or loose connections. Confirm the probe connector is fully seated. Disconnect and reconnect the probe if the design allows normal user-level reconnection. Expected outcome: The device recognizes the probe and completes startup or self-test. If the probe or cable is damaged, remove the device or accessory from service and send it for repair evaluation.

steps.title: Check for Contamination or Fluid Intrusion
steps.instructions: Fluid residue can interfere with buttons, contacts, charging, or probe communication. Inspect the scanner body, probe, charger contacts, and battery area for cleaning fluid, gel buildup, residue, corrosion, or signs of liquid entry. Clean only according to approved facility and manufacturer cleaning practices. Allow the device to dry fully before retesting. Expected outcome: External contamination is removed and the unit starts normally. If fluid intrusion, corrosion, or unusual residue is found inside user-accessible areas, stop troubleshooting and escalate.

steps.title: Check Display, Buttons, and Keypad Response
steps.instructions: Startup may appear failed if the display or buttons are not responding correctly. Confirm the power button responds normally. Check whether buttons feel stuck, damaged, unusually soft, or non-responsive. Observe whether the screen backlight turns on, flickers, or remains blank. Expected outcome: Controls respond normally and the display shows the startup screen. If buttons are stuck or the display remains blank despite confirmed power, remove the unit from service.

steps.title: Restart the Device
steps.instructions: A temporary software lockup may clear with a proper restart. Power the unit off. Wait at least 30 seconds. Power the unit back on. Observe whether startup and self-test complete normally. Expected outcome: The device boots normally and no self-test or calibration error returns. If the failure returns repeatedly, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: Confirm the Device Is Not Being Used Outside Normal Conditions
steps.instructions: Environmental or handling issues can contribute to startup or calibration failures. Confirm the scanner is dry, clean, and at normal room temperature. Do not test immediately after the device has been stored in a very cold, hot, or humid area. Allow the unit to acclimate if it was recently transported or stored outside the clinical area. Expected outcome: The device starts and self-checks normally under normal operating conditions. If the problem resolves after acclimation and drying, document the condition found.

steps.title: Attempt User-Level Calibration Only If Approved
steps.instructions: Do not perform service-level calibration steps unless your department is trained, authorized, and has the required tools. Check whether the issue requires routine user-accessible calibration or a calibration verification process. Use only approved calibration accessories, targets, or procedures available to Clinical Engineering. Do not bypass calibration warnings or clear errors without correcting the cause. Expected outcome: The scanner completes the approved calibration or verification process successfully. If calibration fails again, remove the unit from service.

steps.title: Check for Repeated or Intermittent Startup Failure
steps.instructions: Intermittent failures should be treated seriously even if the device occasionally starts. Power cycle the device several times. Confirm whether the failure happens every time or only intermittently. Check whether the problem changes when the probe cable, charger connection, or battery is gently repositioned. Expected outcome: The device starts consistently without cable movement, power interruption, or repeated errors. If startup depends on cable position, battery movement, or repeated attempts, the device should not be returned to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the Verathon BladderScan BVI 9400 would not complete startup and displayed a calibration or self-test failure before scanning.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the scanner battery charged and the outlet tested good, but the device continued to fail startup/self-test after probe reconnection and restart.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the BladderScan BVI 9400 from service, labeled it Out of Service, and sent it for bench evaluation/vendor repair due to persistent startup/self-test failure.

helpfulDetails: Alarm behavior, including any calibration or self-test message displayed
Accessories swapped, including charging base, power supply, battery, probe, or cable

Power behavior, including outlet tested and confirmed good, battery charge level or charging status, charging base indicator behavior, power supply condition, and whether the failure occurs at startup or during scan setup
Environmental factors, including unusual heat, smell, fluid residue, corrosion, storage temperature, humidity, or whether the issue is constant or intermittent
Indicator lights, including charging base indicator behavior, display behavior, and button/keypad response
Final device status, including whether the device was returned to service, removed from service, labeled Out of Service, or sent for repair evaluation

title: Verathon BladderScan i10 Bladder Scanner - Barcode Scanner or Patient ID Entry Failure
description: Addresses barcode recognition, patient ID entry, scanner connection, label quality, workflow, keyboard, configuration, and interface causes.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Identification Integrity
steps.instructions: Do not save a scan under an uncertain or incorrect patient identity. Pause the workflow and verify the patient using approved identifiers. Use manual entry only when permitted by facility policy and when the patient identity can be confirmed accurately. Expected outcome: No scan is associated with the wrong patient while troubleshooting occurs.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Entry Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The barcode scanner has no power It scans but enters no data It enters incomplete or incorrect characters Manual patient ID entry also fails One barcode type fails while others work The patient record is rejected after entry The problem occurs only in an interfaced workflow Record any displayed message without assuming its cause. Expected outcome: The issue is isolated to scanning, manual entry, data validation, or downstream interface workflow.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Patient Entry Screen
steps.instructions: Confirm that the cursor is active in the intended patient ID field and that the device is not waiting for operator login, required demographics, or another mandatory selection. Exit unrelated menus and return to the normal patient-entry workflow. Expected outcome: The system is ready to accept barcode or manual patient data.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Barcode and Label
steps.instructions: Verify that the barcode is not wrinkled, wet, torn, faded, overly glossy, curved, or covered by tape. Compare with a known-good facility barcode of the same supported type. Do not create or alter patient identifiers outside the approved registration workflow. Expected outcome: A clean, readable, supported barcode is available. If it scans correctly, the original label was the cause.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Barcode Scanner and Connection
steps.instructions: Check the scanner window, cable, connector, strain relief, and accessible port for dirt, damage, looseness, bent contacts, or contamination. Clean the scanner window by the approved method and reseat the connection. Confirm the scanner receives power or gives its normal ready indication. Expected outcome: The scanner is clean, powered, and securely connected. If scanning returns, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 6. Test Scan Technique
steps.instructions: Aim the scanner squarely at the barcode at a reasonable distance. Avoid excessive room glare, direct sunlight, curved wristbands, and rapid movement. Test several known-good labels rather than repeatedly scanning one questionable barcode. Expected outcome: The scanner consistently reads known-good labels when positioned correctly.

steps.title: 7. Test Manual Patient ID Entry
steps.instructions: Use the approved onscreen keyboard or connected input device to enter a test identifier according to facility procedure. Confirm that all characters register correctly and that the field accepts the expected format. Expected outcome: Manual entry works normally. If barcode scanning alone fails, the problem is isolated to the scanner, label, connection, or barcode configuration.

steps.title: 8. Check External Keyboard or Input Device
steps.instructions: If an external keyboard or accessory is used, inspect and reseat its connection. Disconnect nonessential input devices and retest the built-in entry method. Use a known-good approved accessory when available. Expected outcome: Patient data can be entered through at least one approved method, and a faulty external accessory can be isolated.

steps.title: 9. Verify Approved Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm that the patient ID field, barcode workflow, and permitted barcode types match the facility-approved configuration. Do not alter barcode symbology, access control, network, or patient-data configuration without authorization and a documented change process. Expected outcome: The observed configuration matches the approved baseline. Any mismatch is escalated to the authorized system administrator or service provider.

steps.title: 10. Restart and Retest
steps.instructions: Complete or cancel the current workflow safely, restart the scanner, and return to patient entry. Test a known-good barcode and manual entry again. Expected outcome: Patient ID entry works reliably after restart. If the problem returns, further service is required.

steps.title: 11. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify that the device: Reads a known-good barcode Places data in the correct field Accepts approved manual entry Preserves the correct patient association Saves a test record as expected Does not duplicate or truncate the identifier Use nonclinical test data or the approved test workflow. Expected outcome: Patient identification is accurate and repeatable. The device may return to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the barcode scanner illuminated but would not enter the patient ID.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the barcode scanner cable was loose at the scanner interface.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated the cable, scanned multiple approved test barcodes, verified correct field entry, and confirmed normal patient ID workflow.

title: Verathon BladderScan i10 Bladder Scanner - Calibration, Self-Test, or Verification Failure
description: Addresses failed performance checks caused by setup, probe condition, test accessory, positioning, power, environment, procedure, or service-level faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient From Unverified Measurements
steps.instructions: Do not use the scanner for patient-care decisions after a failed calibration, self-test, or performance verification. Provide another verified scanner. Clearly identify the device to prevent clinical reuse until the failure is resolved and documented. Expected outcome: Patient care continues with equipment of verified performance.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Type of Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the failure occurred during: Startup self-test Routine functional verification Calibration procedure Approved phantom or verifier test Post-repair testing A software-generated maintenance prompt Record the exact message, stage, and observed result. Do not invent acceptance limits or repeat procedures without knowing which test failed. Expected outcome: The specific failed process and test stage are identified.

steps.title: 3. Review the Approved Procedure and Equipment
steps.instructions: Confirm that the correct Verathon documentation, approved verifier or phantom, compatible probe, required accessories, and current facility procedure are being used. Check that the test equipment is within its required calibration or verification status. Expected outcome: The correct test method and valid test equipment are confirmed.

steps.title: 4. Verify Stable Power
steps.instructions: Confirm adequate battery charge or connect approved external power. Ensure the device does not dim, restart, or shut down during the test. Do not perform a performance test under unstable power conditions. Expected outcome: The device remains powered and stable throughout the verification process.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Probe
steps.instructions: Inspect the probe surface, housing, cable, strain relief, and connector for cracks, wear, dried gel, contamination, impact damage, or loose connection. Clean and prepare the probe using the approved method. Reseat the connector if applicable. Expected outcome: The probe is clean, intact, and securely connected. If correction allows the test to pass, continue with repeat verification.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Verification Accessory
steps.instructions: Examine the approved phantom, target, stand, or verification accessory for contamination, damage, incorrect assembly, trapped air, missing components, or expired status when applicable. Do not substitute improvised containers or materials. Expected outcome: The verification accessory is suitable, correctly assembled, and ready for use.

steps.title: 7. Check Positioning and Test Setup
steps.instructions: Position the probe and verification accessory exactly as required by the approved procedure. Stabilize both components and avoid movement during acquisition. Confirm that the correct device mode and test selection are active. Expected outcome: The test setup is repeatable and free of positioning error.

steps.title: 8. Check Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Perform the test in a stable indoor environment away from vibration, direct heat, condensation, and strong electromagnetic interference. Allow the device and test accessory to reach the same room environment after transport or storage. Expected outcome: Environmental conditions do not interfere with the test.

steps.title: 9. Repeat the Test Once Using Corrected Setup
steps.instructions: After correcting any external setup issue, repeat the complete test from the beginning. Do not repeatedly retest a failing device in an attempt to obtain a passing result. Expected outcome: The device passes the approved check consistently. A single inconsistent pass is not sufficient for return to service.

steps.title: 10. Compare With a Known-Good Component
steps.instructions: When permitted, compare the device using a known-good compatible probe, approved verifier, or another verified scanner with the same test accessory. This comparison should isolate the scanner, probe, or verification accessory without altering internal calibration data. Expected outcome: The failing component or test setup is narrowed to the scanner, probe, or accessory.

steps.title: 11. Verify Calibration and Configuration Status
steps.instructions: Confirm that the device’s calibration or maintenance status matches the approved service record. Do not change calibration coefficients, enter restricted service menus, or clear maintenance conditions without authorization. Expected outcome: No unauthorized or undocumented configuration change is made. Any service-level calibration requirement is escalated appropriately.

steps.title: 12. Complete Return-to-Service Verification
steps.instructions: A device that passes must complete the full required verification, not only the previously failed portion. Confirm startup, probe recognition, scan completion, result display, data storage, and applicable safety checks. Expected outcome: All required tests pass consistently and are documented before the device returns to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the BladderScan i10 failed its scheduled performance verification.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the approved verification target was contaminated with dried gel and was not positioned correctly.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned and repositioned the test accessory, repeated the approved verification successfully, and completed final functional testing.

title: Verathon BladderScan i10 Bladder Scanner - Cart Power, Dock Power, or Charging Contact Failure
description: Addresses cart or dock charging failure caused by outlet, cord, power supply, seating, contact contamination, alignment, battery, or accessory faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Secure the Equipment
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot cart or dock power while the scanner is needed for active patient care. Move care to another verified scanner. Set the cart brakes and place it on a stable surface before inspecting cords or removing the scanner from its cradle. Expected outcome: Patient care continues and the cart remains stable during troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Charging or Power Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The cart has no power The scanner does not charge in the dock Charging is intermittent Charging stops when the cart moves The scanner powers from direct AC but not the dock Another accessory on the cart also lacks power The dock indicator is absent or abnormal Observe the scanner and cart indicators without relying only on the battery icon. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to the cart, dock, contact path, scanner, or building power source.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Wall Outlet
steps.instructions: Test the outlet using an approved outlet tester or known-good device. Confirm that any wall switch, emergency-power designation, power strip, or isolation system is in the intended state. Do not use damaged receptacles or unauthorized extension cords. Expected outcome: A stable AC source is confirmed. If outlet correction restores charging, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Cart Power Cord
steps.instructions: Inspect the full accessible length of the power cord, plug, strain relief, cart inlet, and cord retention for cuts, crushing, exposed conductors, loose blades, discoloration, or heat damage. Remove the cart from service immediately if electrical damage is found. Expected outcome: The cord and inlet are intact and securely connected.

steps.title: 5. Check the Cart Power Supply and Indicators
steps.instructions: Confirm that the cart power supply is connected and that its normal indicators are present. Inspect low-voltage cables and accessible connectors for looseness, contamination, and damage. Do not open the power supply enclosure. Expected outcome: The cart power supply receives AC and provides normal external indication.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Dock Seating
steps.instructions: Remove the scanner and inspect the cradle for foreign objects, damaged guides, bent components, dried gel, or accessories preventing full seating. Reinstall the scanner squarely and verify that it settles completely into the charging position. Expected outcome: The scanner is fully seated and charging begins. If so, continue to final testing.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Charging Contacts
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible contacts on the scanner and dock for debris, gel, oxidation, wear, recessed pins, misalignment, or physical damage. Clean only according to the approved external cleaning process. Do not scrape contacts with metal tools or apply unapproved chemicals. Expected outcome: Contacts are clean, aligned, and able to make consistent connection.

steps.title: 8. Check for Intermittency
steps.instructions: With the scanner properly seated, observe charging status while lightly stabilizing the cart and cable. Do not aggressively move or flex the equipment. If charging changes with slight movement, inspect cable routing, strain reliefs, dock alignment, and contact engagement. Expected outcome: Charging remains stable during normal cart handling.

steps.title: 9. Compare Direct and Docked Charging
steps.instructions: When the design permits, connect the scanner using an approved direct charging method and compare it with dock charging. A scanner that charges directly but not through the dock points toward the cart, dock, contacts, or cart power path. Expected outcome: The affected part of the charging path is isolated without internal disassembly.

steps.title: 10. Remove Nonessential Cart Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential approved peripherals from the cart power system and retest charging. A damaged accessory or overloaded cart power path may interfere with normal operation. Reconnect accessories one at a time after stable charging is confirmed. Expected outcome: The scanner charges normally with nonessential accessories removed, or the failure remains isolated to the dock or power system.

steps.title: 11. Compare With a Known-Good Component
steps.instructions: When approved compatible equipment is available, test the scanner in a known-good dock or test the dock with a known-good scanner. Clearly identify all units and avoid mixing unapproved accessories. Expected outcome: The failed scanner, dock, cart power system, or battery is isolated.

steps.title: 12. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm that: Cart and dock indicators are normal Charging begins each time the scanner is seated The displayed battery state increases Charging remains stable during normal cart movement The scanner operates on battery after charging A test scan completes normally No cord, contact, or power component overheats Expected outcome: Cart power, dock power, and charging contact operation are stable. The system may return to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the BladderScan i10 did not charge when placed in the cart dock.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried gel on the dock contacts that prevented consistent electrical contact.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned the accessible charging contacts, reseated the scanner, verified stable charging and battery operation, and completed a successful test scan.

title: Verathon BladderScan i10 Bladder Scanner - Device Will Not Power On or Unexpectedly Shuts Down
description: Addresses no-power, intermittent shutdown, depleted battery, AC power, docking, charging-contact, accessory, and environmental causes before service escalation.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Continuity of Care
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot the scanner while it is required for an active patient assessment. Move the examination to another verified bladder scanner or follow the approved clinical alternative. Inspect for liquid intrusion, impact damage, overheating, smoke, odor, exposed conductors, or a swollen battery condition. Remove the device from service immediately if any unsafe condition is present. Expected outcome: Patient care continues with verified equipment, and the i10 is safe for external evaluation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Power Condition
steps.instructions: Ask whether the device: Does not respond at all Starts and immediately shuts down Shuts down only during scanning Operates on AC or dock power but not battery Operates on battery but not through the cart or dock Shuts down after being moved or handled Attempt a normal power-on using the approved control. Observe the display, indicators, sounds, and any startup messages. Expected outcome: The exact failure mode and power source involved are identified. If the device starts and remains stable, continue with functional verification.

steps.title: 3. Check the External Power Source
steps.instructions: Verify that the wall outlet is active using an approved outlet tester or known-good device. Confirm that any switched outlet, power strip, isolation system, or cart power control is turned on. Avoid using damaged extension cords, unauthorized adapters, or overloaded receptacles. Expected outcome: A stable and appropriate AC source is confirmed. If correcting the outlet restores reliable operation, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Power Supply and Cables
steps.instructions: Inspect the external power supply, AC cord, low-voltage cable, connectors, strain reliefs, and plug blades for damage, contamination, looseness, pin deformation, or intermittent connection. Reseat each accessible connection. Confirm that the power supply is the approved type assigned to the device or cart. Expected outcome: All external power components are secure and undamaged. If reseating a connection restores stable operation, proceed to final functional testing.

steps.title: 5. Evaluate Battery and Charging Status
steps.instructions: Place the device on its approved charging system or connect approved external power. Observe whether charging indicators appear and whether the displayed battery state increases. Allow sufficient charging time before evaluating short runtime. Do not assume battery failure when the charger, dock, contacts, or outlet have not been verified. Expected outcome: Charging begins normally and the device remains powered. If the battery accepts charge and supports normal operation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Docking and Charging Contacts
steps.instructions: Remove the device from the dock or cart cradle. Inspect accessible charging contacts for debris, dried gel, oxidation, misalignment, recessed pins, or physical damage. Clean only by the approved external cleaning method. Reinstall the device squarely and confirm that it fully seats without obstruction. Expected outcome: Contacts are clean, aligned, and making reliable connection. If charging or power operation returns, proceed to final testing.

steps.title: 7. Isolate the Device From Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential external accessories such as printers, barcode scanners, USB devices, network cables, or other approved peripherals. Restart the scanner and observe whether it remains powered without the accessories connected. Reconnect accessories one at a time if operation is stable. Expected outcome: The scanner remains powered with nonessential accessories removed. A specific accessory or cable can be isolated if shutdown returns after reconnection.

steps.title: 8. Check for Environmental Causes
steps.instructions: Confirm that ventilation openings are unobstructed and that the device is not exposed to excessive heat, condensation, direct fluid spray, or rapid temperature change. Allow equipment moved from a cold or humid location to reach the clinical environment before testing. Expected outcome: The device operates in a suitable environment without overheating or moisture-related instability.

steps.title: 9. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: With the patient disconnected from the workflow, shut the scanner down normally. Disconnect external power, remove it from the charging dock, wait briefly, reconnect approved power, and restart. Do not use unauthorized reset procedures or enter restricted service menus. Expected outcome: The scanner completes startup and remains stable. If it repeatedly resets, freezes, or shuts down, remove it from service.

steps.title: 10. Complete Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm that the scanner: Powers on from the intended source Remains on without interruption Recognizes charging status Starts and completes a test scan using an approved test method Saves or displays results normally Shows no abnormal heat, odor, or warning condition Expected outcome: Normal power and scanning functions are verified. The device may return to service only when operation is stable and all required checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the BladderScan i10 shut down during use and would not remain powered on.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the scanner was not fully seated in the cart dock because dried gel contaminated the charging contacts.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned the accessible contacts, reseated the scanner, verified charging, completed a test scan, and confirmed stable operation.

helpfulDetails: Whether the device was on battery, dock, or AC power
Any heat, odor, noise, or damage

title: Verathon BladderScan i10 Bladder Scanner - Patient Record Storage Full or Saved Scan Retrieval Failure
description: Addresses full storage, missing saved scans, filters, patient selection, permissions, date settings, synchronization, and record-management causes.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Data Integrity
steps.instructions: Do not delete records, clear storage, reset the device, or alter patient information until retention requirements and data-transfer status are confirmed. Use another verified scanner if new scans cannot be safely saved or correctly associated with the patient. Expected outcome: Existing patient records are protected while troubleshooting proceeds.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Record Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether: New scans cannot be saved A storage-full warning appears One patient record is missing All saved records are unavailable Records appear under the wrong date or patient Retrieval fails only after login Records are present locally but not in an external system Record the exact message and workflow used. Expected outcome: The issue is isolated to saving, local retrieval, filtering, permissions, date indexing, or external transfer.

steps.title: 3. Verify Patient and Search Criteria
steps.instructions: Confirm the patient identifier, operator, date range, record type, and other visible filters. Clear unnecessary filters using normal user controls. Search using a known recent test record or a record whose details are confirmed. Expected outcome: The intended record appears when correct search criteria are used. If so, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Check Date and Time
steps.instructions: Verify that the scanner’s displayed date and time are correct. An incorrect clock may place saved scans outside the expected search range. Do not change protected time synchronization or network settings without authorization. Expected outcome: The device time is accurate or the record is located under the date when it was actually stored.

steps.title: 5. Verify User Access
steps.instructions: Confirm that the logged-in operator has permission to view, retrieve, or manage the required records. Test using an authorized account according to facility procedure. Do not share credentials or bypass access controls. Expected outcome: Authorized users can access the expected record functions.

steps.title: 6. Review Storage Status
steps.instructions: Use the normal information or record-management screen to check whether storage is near capacity or full. Do not assume that deleting one record is an acceptable solution. Confirm whether records have been successfully exported, printed, archived, or transferred before any authorized deletion. Expected outcome: The available storage condition is known and data retention requirements remain protected.

steps.title: 7. Verify Save Completion
steps.instructions: Create a nonclinical test record using the approved test workflow. Confirm that the device indicates a successful save and that the record can immediately be retrieved. Do not create test data under a real patient. Expected outcome: New records save and retrieve normally. If the test record works, the issue may be limited to earlier records, filters, or patient identifiers.

steps.title: 8. Check External Data Transfer Status
steps.instructions: If records are expected to transfer to another system, verify that the network, interface, destination, and queue are available. Confirm whether the record remains on the device, is pending, or transferred successfully. Do not delete local records merely because the external system has not displayed them. Expected outcome: The local and external record locations are understood, and transfer failure is distinguished from local storage failure.

steps.title: 9. Restart and Recheck Records
steps.instructions: Exit the patient workflow and restart the scanner normally. Log in with an authorized account and repeat the record search. Do not perform factory resets, database repair, or storage formatting. Expected outcome: Saved records and storage functions return after restart. If retrieval remains unreliable, remove the device from service.

steps.title: 10. Follow Authorized Data-Management Procedures
steps.instructions: If storage is confirmed full, follow the facility-approved and manufacturer-supported process for exporting, archiving, or deleting eligible records. Verify successful transfer and required retention before removing any data. Maintain an audit trail when required. Expected outcome: Space is restored without losing required clinical records, and new records save normally.

steps.title: 11. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm that the scanner can: Save a test scan Retrieve the same scan Search by approved criteria Display correct patient information Preserve date and time Transfer or print the record when required Report available storage normally Expected outcome: Record storage and retrieval are accurate, repeatable, and compliant. The device may return to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that recent saved bladder scans could not be found in the patient record list.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the record search was limited by an incorrect date filter after the device clock had been corrected.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering updated the search range, located the records, saved and retrieved a test scan, and verified normal record access.

helpfulDetails: Patient ID and search criteria used

title: Verathon BladderScan i10 Bladder Scanner - Printer or Report Output Failure
description: Addresses missing reports, printer power, paper, connection, queue, selection, configuration, accessory, and workflow causes.

steps.title: 1. Protect Clinical Documentation
steps.instructions: Do not assume a report printed or transferred successfully. Verify that the scan result remains visible or saved and document the result through an approved alternate method when necessary. Do not delay patient care solely to troubleshoot a printer. Expected outcome: The scan result is preserved and available through an approved documentation path.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Output Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: Nothing prints The printer is not recognized A blank or partial report prints Printing stops midway The wrong patient or report prints The report remains queued Electronic export fails while local printing works Record indicator lights and displayed messages. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to printer hardware, report selection, queue, formatting, or electronic output.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Report and Destination
steps.instructions: Confirm that the intended patient, scan, report type, and output destination are selected. Check that the user is not sending the report to an unavailable or disabled destination. Expected outcome: The correct report is selected and directed to the intended approved output.

steps.title: 4. Check Printer Power
steps.instructions: Verify that the printer or cart printer is turned on and receiving power. Inspect its approved power supply, cable, cart power connection, and outlet. Confirm normal ready indicators and no visible damage or overheating. Expected outcome: The printer has stable power and is in a ready state.

steps.title: 5. Check Paper or Media
steps.instructions: Inspect the paper supply, roll orientation, cover closure, feed path, and accessible cutter area. Remove visible jams using the approved external method. Use only approved paper or media. Do not insert tools into the print mechanism. Expected outcome: Paper is correctly loaded, the cover is secure, and the feed path is clear.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Data Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect and reseat the printer data cable, USB connection, dock connection, or other approved interface. Check for damaged connectors, bent contacts, contamination, or strain. Disconnect and reconnect only when the workflow is not actively transferring data. Expected outcome: The printer communication path is secure and undamaged.

steps.title: 7. Test the Printer Independently
steps.instructions: Use the printer’s approved self-test or feed function when available. This distinguishes printer mechanics and power from scanner communication. Do not access internal printer service menus. Expected outcome: The printer feeds or completes its approved self-test. If it does not, remove the printer from service.

steps.title: 8. Retry From a Known-Good Saved Record
steps.instructions: Select a nonclinical test record or approved saved scan and send it to the printer once. Avoid repeatedly submitting the same job, which may create duplicate reports. Expected outcome: One complete report prints with correct patient and scan information.

steps.title: 9. Clear a Visible Output Queue Safely
steps.instructions: If the normal user interface shows stalled or duplicate jobs, cancel only the affected test job using approved controls. Do not delete clinical records or clear system data without authorization. Expected outcome: The queue returns to a ready state and a new test report processes normally.

steps.title: 10. Compare With a Known-Good Printer or Cable
steps.instructions: When approved compatible equipment is available, test with a known-good cable or printer. Clearly identify the original accessory to prevent accidental reuse. Expected outcome: Successful output with the substitute isolates the original printer or cable. Failure with both suggests scanner configuration or interface issues.

steps.title: 11. Verify Approved Output Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm that the configured printer or report destination matches the facility-approved setup. Do not change drivers, network destinations, templates, or protected settings without authorization. Expected outcome: The output configuration matches the approved baseline or is escalated to the authorized administrator.

steps.title: 12. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Print or export an approved test report. Confirm: Correct patient or test identity Complete scan result Legible output Correct date and time No duplicate pages Successful saved-record retrieval Ready status after completion Expected outcome: Report output is complete, accurate, and repeatable. The system may return to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that completed bladder scans would not print from the cart printer.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the printer paper roll was installed in the incorrect orientation.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reloaded the approved paper correctly, printed a complete test report, and verified accurate patient and scan information.

title: Verathon BladderScan i10 Bladder Scanner - Probe Scan Button Not Responding
description: Addresses an unresponsive probe button caused by connection, contamination, control lock, workflow, cable, probe, or software conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Assessment Capability
steps.instructions: Do not continue using an unreliable scan control during a patient examination. Use another verified scanner or an approved alternate scan control only if it is designed for clinical use. Remove the probe from use if the button is physically damaged, sticking, cracked, or contaminated internally. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without depending on an unreliable control.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Button Failure
steps.instructions: Verify whether the button: Does not move Moves but gives no response Works intermittently Requires unusual pressure Fails only at certain screens Fails when the cable is moved Observe whether another approved scan control can start acquisition. Expected outcome: The failure is confirmed as mechanical, intermittent, workflow-related, or isolated to the probe control.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Device Is Scan Ready
steps.instructions: Confirm that the scanner is powered, logged in if required, on the correct patient or exam screen, and not displaying a prompt that must be completed. Verify that scanning is not disabled by an active menu, dialog, access restriction, or incomplete patient entry. Expected outcome: The scanner is in a state where the probe button should initiate a scan.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Button Externally
steps.instructions: Inspect around the button for dried gel, cleaning residue, adhesive, a torn membrane, impact damage, or material preventing normal travel. Clean only by the approved external method. Do not pry, remove the button cover, or introduce fluid into the probe. Expected outcome: The button moves freely and is externally clean. If cleaning restores response, proceed to final testing.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Probe Cable and Connector
steps.instructions: Check the cable, strain relief, connector, and accessible contacts for cuts, kinks, crushed areas, looseness, contamination, or movement-related intermittency. Reseat the probe connection without forcing it. Route the cable so it is not under tension. Expected outcome: The probe is securely connected and the button response is stable.

steps.title: 6. Compare With an Alternate Approved Scan Control
steps.instructions: Use the scanner’s alternate approved scan-start control, when available. If the alternate control initiates and completes scans, the core scanner and acquisition path are likely operational. Do not use unauthorized keyboard commands or service functions. Expected outcome: Successful scanning from the alternate control isolates the issue to the probe button, cable, or probe assembly.

steps.title: 7. Compare With a Known-Good Probe
steps.instructions: When the probe is detachable and an approved compatible probe is available, connect the known-good probe and test its scan button. Keep the original probe clearly identified to prevent accidental clinical reuse. Expected outcome: A working known-good probe confirms that the original probe assembly requires service. If neither button works, evaluate scanner software or interface conditions.

steps.title: 8. Restart the Scanner
steps.instructions: Exit the patient workflow, shut down normally, restart the scanner, and return to the scan-ready screen. Do not enter restricted service menus or alter protected configuration. Expected outcome: The button is recognized after restart. If the failure returns, the device or probe must be removed from service.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Initiate and complete multiple scans using the probe button. Confirm normal button travel, immediate command recognition, complete acquisition, and no response interruption when the cable is gently repositioned. Expected outcome: The probe button operates reliably through repeated tests. Troubleshooting can stop and the device may return to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that pressing the probe scan button did not start bladder scan acquisition.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried ultrasound gel restricting normal movement of the probe button.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned the probe exterior using the approved method, verified normal button travel, and completed repeated successful test scans.

title: Verathon BladderScan i10 Bladder Scanner - Scan Will Not Start or Acquisition Stops Before Completion
description: Addresses scan initiation, interrupted acquisition, probe connection, positioning, gel, controls, battery, patient selection, and environmental causes.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Continue Care
steps.instructions: Do not delay necessary assessment while troubleshooting. Use another verified bladder scanner or the approved clinical alternative if the scan is clinically time-sensitive. Do not continue using equipment that repeatedly stops, produces unreliable acquisitions, or has visible probe or cable damage. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely while the scanner is evaluated away from active dependence.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Scan Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The scan control does nothing Acquisition begins but stops The image appears but no result is calculated The problem occurs with one operator or all operators The failure occurs with one patient, body type, or position A message appears before or during acquisition Repeat the sequence using the normal clinical workflow without changing restricted settings. Expected outcome: The failure point is clearly identified. If the scan completes normally, perform repeat verification before returning the device to service.

steps.title: 3. Verify Device Power and Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm that the scanner is fully powered, not in a low-power state, and has adequate battery charge. Connect approved power or place the device in its charging system if the battery is low. Observe for dimming, restarting, or shutdown when acquisition begins. Expected outcome: Stable power is available throughout the scan. If charging resolves the interruption, complete final verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Correct Patient and Exam Workflow
steps.instructions: Confirm that the required patient, operator, exam, or mode selections have been completed and that no mandatory field is preventing scan initiation. Do not alter protected configuration or access-control settings without authorization. Expected outcome: The device is at the normal scan-ready screen with all required workflow entries completed.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Probe and External Cable Path
steps.instructions: Inspect the probe, cable, connector, strain relief, and accessible connection points for cuts, kinks, contamination, looseness, bent contacts, or impact damage. Reseat any accessible connector using the approved method. Do not twist or force connectors. Expected outcome: The probe path is intact and securely connected. If reseating restores scanning, continue to final testing.

steps.title: 6. Check the Probe Scan Button
steps.instructions: Press the probe scan button deliberately and observe whether the device acknowledges the command. Compare operation with any alternate approved scan control available on the system. If one control starts scanning and the probe button does not, isolate the issue to the button, cable, or probe assembly. Expected outcome: The scan command is recognized. If the alternate control works reliably, remove the affected probe or control from service as appropriate.

steps.title: 7. Verify Probe Preparation and Gel Application
steps.instructions: Confirm that the probe surface is clean, undamaged, and prepared according to the approved clinical process. Apply an appropriate amount of approved ultrasound gel and eliminate large air gaps. Remove dried gel or residue that may interfere with acoustic coupling. Expected outcome: The probe has consistent contact and a usable acoustic path. If acquisition completes after proper preparation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 8. Check Patient and Probe Positioning
steps.instructions: Confirm that the patient is positioned appropriately and that the probe is centered and oriented correctly over the expected bladder location. Avoid excessive probe movement during acquisition. Consider whether dressings, anatomy, recent surgery, catheters, body habitus, or patient movement may affect acquisition. Expected outcome: The probe remains stable and the device receives a consistent signal through the complete scan.

steps.title: 9. Remove External Interference
steps.instructions: Move the device away from equipment producing strong vibration or electromagnetic interference. Ensure that the cart is stable and that the probe cable is not being pulled during scanning. Disconnect nonessential peripherals temporarily and repeat the scan. Expected outcome: Acquisition completes without environmental or accessory-related interruption.

steps.title: 10. Compare With a Known-Good Probe When Authorized
steps.instructions: If the probe is detachable and an approved compatible probe is available, connect a known-good probe and repeat the scan using an approved test method. Do not interchange incompatible probes or accessories. Expected outcome: A successful scan with the known-good probe isolates the original probe or cable. If both probes fail, the scanner requires further evaluation.

steps.title: 11. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Complete several test acquisitions using an approved phantom, verifier, or facility test method. Confirm that each scan starts, progresses, completes, displays a result, and can be saved as expected. Expected outcome: Repeated acquisitions complete without interruption. The device can return to service when scan reliability is verified.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that scans began normally but stopped before a bladder volume result was displayed.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the probe connector was partially unseated and lost communication when the cable moved.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated the probe connector, secured the cable routing, completed repeated test scans, and verified normal acquisition.

title: Verathon BladderScan i10 Bladder Scanner - Software Update or Configuration Transfer Failure
description: Addresses failed updates or configuration transfers caused by power, media, files, connection, compatibility, authorization, or network conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Device and Clinical Workflow
steps.instructions: Remove the scanner from clinical use before starting or troubleshooting an update or configuration transfer. Provide another verified scanner for patient care. Do not interrupt power, remove media, disconnect cables, or restart the device while an update is actively applying unless approved recovery instructions specifically require it. Expected outcome: Patient care continues and the device is protected from an incomplete update.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Failed Process
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves: Software download Update-file recognition Installation start Installation interruption Restart after update Configuration export Configuration import Transfer between devices Network-based deployment Record the exact message, file source, step reached, and current software state. Expected outcome: The failure is identified as file, media, communication, authorization, installation, or restart related.

steps.title: 3. Verify Authorization and Change Control
steps.instructions: Confirm that the update or configuration transfer is approved by the facility and supported for the exact BladderScan i10 hardware and current software version. Verify that the installer, configuration package, or instructions came from an authorized source. Expected outcome: The planned change is authorized, applicable, and traceable.

steps.title: 4. Confirm Stable Power
steps.instructions: Connect the scanner to approved external power and verify charging or power indicators. Ensure that the cart, dock, outlet, and power supply are stable. Do not perform an update using a depleted battery or intermittent dock connection. Expected outcome: Stable power is available for the entire update and restart process.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Transfer Media or Cable
steps.instructions: Inspect the approved USB device, cable, port, or network connection for damage, contamination, looseness, or improper seating. Do not use unknown, unapproved, encrypted, or damaged media. Expected outcome: The transfer path is secure and physically intact.

steps.title: 6. Verify the File or Package
steps.instructions: Confirm the file name, version, package structure, media location, and compatibility against approved documentation. Verify that the file was fully copied and not renamed, compressed, or altered unexpectedly. Do not modify update files or configuration packages. Expected outcome: The device is presented with a complete and compatible package.

steps.title: 7. Check Available Storage
steps.instructions: Using normal system information screens, confirm that adequate storage is available for the update or transfer. Do not delete patient records or system files to create space unless an authorized data-management procedure has been completed. Expected outcome: Storage capacity is not preventing the process.

steps.title: 8. Check User Access and Administrative Rights
steps.instructions: Confirm that the logged-in account has the authorized permission to perform the update or configuration transfer. Do not use shared credentials, bypass access control, or attempt unauthorized privilege escalation. Expected outcome: The process is initiated under the correct authorized account.

steps.title: 9. Retry From a Known-Good Source
steps.instructions: When approved, copy the authorized package to known-good compatible media or use a verified cable or network connection. Repeat the process from the beginning according to the approved instructions. Expected outcome: The device recognizes and completes the transfer. If the same failure recurs, stop repeated attempts.

steps.title: 10. Verify Configuration Scope
steps.instructions: For configuration transfer, confirm that the source and destination devices are the correct models and approved software levels. Review which settings are intended to transfer. Do not overwrite site-specific network, security, patient-data, or access settings without documented approval. Expected outcome: Only the intended compatible configuration is transferred.

steps.title: 11. Observe the Restart and Post-Update State
steps.instructions: After a completed update, allow the device to restart normally. Confirm that it reaches the normal startup screen and displays the intended approved software or configuration state. Do not repeatedly power cycle a device stuck during update recovery. Expected outcome: The scanner starts normally with the approved version or configuration.

steps.title: 12. Complete Return-to-Service Verification
steps.instructions: Verify: Normal startup User login Probe recognition Scan initiation and completion Patient ID entry Record saving and retrieval Printer or interface functions when applicable Date, time, and approved configuration No update or configuration warning Expected outcome: The scanner functions normally with the approved change and may return to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical Engineering reported that the BladderScan i10 would not recognize the approved software update package.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the update file had been copied into an incorrect folder on the approved USB device.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering placed the authorized package in the required media location, completed the update, and verified startup, scanning, record storage, and approved configuration.

title: Verathon BladderScan i10 Bladder Scanner - User Login, Operator ID, or Access Control Failure
description: Addresses login rejection, missing operator access, locked accounts, ID entry, barcode, role assignment, time, network, and configuration causes.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient and User Identity
steps.instructions: Do not share credentials, use another person’s account, bypass access controls, or save scans under an incorrect operator identity. Use another verified scanner or approved downtime workflow if authorized access cannot be restored promptly. Expected outcome: Patient and operator records remain accurate and secure.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Access Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The username or operator ID is rejected The password is rejected The account is locked Barcode login fails The login screen is unresponsive The user can log in but lacks required functions All users are affected Access fails only when the network is unavailable Record the displayed message and affected account without recording passwords. Expected outcome: The issue is isolated to one account, input method, permissions, device configuration, or shared infrastructure.

steps.title: 3. Verify Login Entry
steps.instructions: Confirm the correct username, operator ID format, capitalization, and required domain or site selection when applicable. Use the approved input method and ensure that no extra spaces or unintended characters are entered. Expected outcome: Correct credentials are entered in the expected format.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Input Method
steps.instructions: Test the onscreen keyboard, barcode scanner, or approved external keyboard. Confirm that each character or barcode value enters correctly. Inspect and reseat accessory connections if an external input device is used. Expected outcome: The login failure is not caused by missing, duplicated, or incorrect input characters.

steps.title: 5. Test a Different Authorized Account
steps.instructions: Have another authorized user attempt login according to facility policy. Do not expose or exchange passwords. If another account works, the issue is likely isolated to the original account or assigned role. Expected outcome: Device-wide access failure is distinguished from a single-user account issue.

steps.title: 6. Check Account Status Through the Authorized Administrator
steps.instructions: Have the authorized system administrator verify whether the account is active, locked, expired, disabled, or assigned to the correct role. Clinical Engineering should not change clinical access rights without approved authorization. Expected outcome: The account status and role assignment are confirmed and corrected through the proper process.

steps.title: 7. Verify Date and Time
steps.instructions: Check the scanner’s date and time. Significant clock errors may interfere with authentication, certificate validation, or synchronized account access. Do not alter protected synchronization settings without authorization. Expected outcome: The device time is correct or the time issue is escalated to the authorized administrator.

steps.title: 8. Check Network Availability When Required
steps.instructions: If login depends on a network or central user directory, verify link status, Wi-Fi or wired connectivity, approved network profile, and availability of the related authentication service. Compare with another device on the same approved network when appropriate. Expected outcome: The authentication path is available, or an infrastructure issue is identified for escalation.

steps.title: 9. Review Approved Access Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm that login requirements, operator ID settings, and role-based access match the facility-approved configuration. Do not disable login, create unauthorized accounts, or reduce security controls to restore access. Expected outcome: Access-control configuration is verified without compromising security.

steps.title: 10. Restart and Retest
steps.instructions: Safely exit the workflow, restart the scanner, and attempt login using an authorized test account. Do not perform a factory reset or clear user data. Expected outcome: Login functions normally after restart. If failure returns, remove the device from service when required.

steps.title: 11. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Using an authorized account, confirm: Successful login Correct operator identity displayed Access only to permitted functions Successful patient ID entry Completion and saving of a test scan Correct operator association in the saved record Normal logout Expected outcome: Access control and operator attribution are accurate and repeatable. The device may return to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that an authorized operator could not log in to the BladderScan i10.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering confirmed that the operator account had become locked after repeated unsuccessful login attempts.
CCR.Resolution: The authorized administrator unlocked the account, and Clinical Engineering verified login, permitted functions, test scanning, and correct operator attribution.

helpfulDetails: Single user or all users affected

title: Verathon GlideScope Video Laryngoscope - Battery Not Charging or Short Runtime
description: Addresses charging failure or reduced runtime caused by AC power, adapter, dock, connection, battery age, storage, or internal charging faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain a Powered Backup
steps.instructions: Do not rely on a GlideScope system with an uncertain battery during airway care. Use another verified device or operate from an approved reliable AC source only when the configuration permits and cable placement is safe. Remove the unit from clinical availability if it shuts down unexpectedly or cannot maintain power. Expected outcome: Patient care is not dependent on an unreliable battery.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Ask whether the battery does not charge, charges slowly, shows a full indication but runs briefly, or causes unexpected shutdown. Record whether the issue occurs on the monitor, portable unit, handle, or another battery-powered component within the specific GlideScope configuration. Reproduce the complaint after a documented charging attempt. Expected outcome: The affected battery-powered component and exact symptom are identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify the AC Source
steps.instructions: Test the wall outlet with an approved outlet tester or a known-good device according to facility policy. Confirm any switched receptacle is on and the plug is fully inserted. Do not use damaged extension cords or unapproved power strips. Expected outcome: A verified AC source is available. If charging begins on a known-good outlet, the original power source is referred for correction.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Approved Power Adapter and Cord
steps.instructions: Check the adapter, cord, plug, and strain reliefs for cuts, loose sections, bent contacts, overheating, discoloration, or incorrect labeling. Confirm the adapter is the approved type for the device. Expected outcome: The power adapter and cord are correct and undamaged. Any unsafe adapter is removed from service.

steps.title: 5. Verify Charging Connection or Docking
steps.instructions: Ensure the charging plug is fully seated or the device is correctly positioned in its charging dock. Inspect contacts for debris, moisture, corrosion, or physical damage. Clean external contacts only through approved methods and allow them to dry fully. Expected outcome: The device makes a secure charging connection and displays the expected charging indication. If charging resumes normally, continue to runtime verification.

steps.title: 6. Observe Charge Indicators
steps.instructions: Record the charging icon, indicator light, battery level, or any displayed message before and after connecting AC power. Allow sufficient observation time to determine whether the state changes. Do not invent charging limits or expected duration; use the applicable manufacturer documentation. Expected outcome: The device recognizes external power and shows an increasing charge state.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Runtime Check
steps.instructions: After charging according to approved instructions, operate the system in a nonclinical test condition. Observe whether the battery level declines unusually quickly or the unit shuts down. Do not intentionally deplete the battery if this conflicts with facility policy or manufacturer guidance. Expected outcome: The system remains powered for an acceptable service period based on manufacturer guidance and facility expectations.

steps.title: 8. Test With a Known-Good Approved Power Accessory
