steps.instructions: Substitute a known-good approved power adapter, cable, or charging dock one item at a time. Expected outcome: Charging with the known-good accessory identifies the original external power accessory as defective.

steps.title: 9. Evaluate Battery Condition Within Authorized Limits
steps.instructions: Review the device age, battery replacement history, storage condition, and prior runtime complaints. Inspect for swelling, leakage, heat, odor, or enclosure distortion. Do not open a sealed battery or replace it unless the procedure is authorized and within the technician’s scope. Expected outcome: A battery showing damage or confirmed inadequate capacity is removed from service and replaced through an approved process.

steps.title: 10. Complete Return-to-Service Verification
steps.instructions: Verify charging indication, battery level increase, stable AC operation, stable battery operation, startup, live image, and no unexpected shutdown. Perform required safety testing after any power-related repair. Expected outcome: The device charges normally and maintains reliable operation. It may return to service only after all required checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GlideScope showed a low battery shortly after being removed from the charger.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the charging plug was not fully seated and the unit had not been charging.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated the approved power connection, confirmed the charge level increased, and verified stable battery operation during a controlled functional test.

helpfulDetails: Battery level before and after charging

title: Verathon GlideScope Video Laryngoscope - Camera Lens Fogging or Persistent Blurred Image
description: Addresses blurred or fogged images caused by contamination, moisture, temperature transition, accessory positioning, damage, or imaging-component failure.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Provide Alternate Visualization
steps.instructions: Do not continue relying on an image that does not provide adequate airway visualization. Move to another verified laryngoscope or airway visualization method before troubleshooting. Handle contaminated reusable components according to infection prevention requirements. Expected outcome: Airway care continues with a clear, reliable visualization method.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Type and Timing of Image Degradation
steps.instructions: Ask whether the image is fogged immediately, becomes blurry after insertion, remains blurred after cleaning, or affects only part of the field. Determine whether the condition appears on one imaging component or all components used with the monitor. Reproduce the condition away from patient care when possible. Expected outcome: The symptom is identified as surface fogging, persistent blur, contamination, or an electronic display problem.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Camera Window Externally
steps.instructions: Under good lighting, inspect the camera window for residue, dried cleaning solution, adhesive, scratches, cracks, moisture, or discoloration. Do not scrape the window or use unapproved abrasive materials. Expected outcome: The camera window is visibly clean and intact. Any cracked or deeply scratched component is removed from service.

steps.title: 4. Clean and Dry the Imaging Component Correctly
steps.instructions: Clean and disinfect the camera, baton, or handle according to the applicable approved procedure. Pay particular attention to the optical window and adjacent surfaces. Allow the component and connectors to dry fully before reconnecting it. Residual moisture or cleaning film can create persistent blur. Expected outcome: The optical surface is clean, dry, and free of residue. If the image becomes clear and remains clear, complete final verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Check for Temperature-Related Condensation
steps.instructions: Determine whether the component was moved directly from a cold storage area into a warm, humid clinical space. Allow it to reach the appropriate room environment before testing. Do not use external heating methods unless specifically approved for the device configuration. Expected outcome: Temporary external condensation clears after environmental stabilization.

steps.title: 6. Verify Compatible Accessory Installation
steps.instructions: Confirm any blade, protective cover, sleeve, or related accessory is compatible and installed in the correct position. Check that plastic film, packaging, residue, or accessory misalignment is not covering the camera window. Expected outcome: The optical path is unobstructed and the accessory is correctly positioned.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Display and Image Settings
steps.instructions: Verify that display brightness or image settings are not creating the appearance of poor focus or low contrast. Compare live menu text or interface graphics with the camera image. If menus are sharp but the live image is blurred, the issue is more likely within the optical path or imaging component. Expected outcome: The display itself is sharp and readable, separating an optical problem from a monitor display problem.

steps.title: 8. Test With a Known-Good Imaging Component
steps.instructions: Connect a known-good compatible camera, video baton, or handle to the same monitor and cable. Follow required cleaning and disinfection practices before substitution. Expected outcome: A clear image with the known-good component identifies the original imaging component as defective or contaminated.

steps.title: 9. Compare the Suspect Component on Another Monitor
steps.instructions: When available, test the suspect component on another verified compatible GlideScope system. Expected outcome: The blur follows the component or remains with the original monitor. Remove the defective component or monitor from service accordingly.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Image Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm a clear image at normal working distance, across normal movement, and after the system has operated long enough to cover the reported fogging period. Verify the image remains usable and free of persistent haze. Expected outcome: The live image remains clear, stable, and clinically usable. The system may return to service only after all required checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GlideScope image remained hazy after the camera was connected.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried cleaning residue covering the external camera window.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned and fully dried the optical window according to approved procedures and verified a clear, stable live image.

title: Verathon GlideScope Video Laryngoscope - Charging Dock or Power Adapter Failure
description: Addresses failed charging caused by the outlet, adapter, cord, dock alignment, contaminated contacts, damage, or internal power faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove Questionable Power Equipment
steps.instructions: Do not use a damaged power adapter or charging dock near a patient. Disconnect any accessory showing exposed conductors, sparking, overheating, liquid intrusion, odor, or enclosure damage. Keep a verified GlideScope system and backup airway method available for clinical use. Expected outcome: Unsafe power accessories are isolated, and patient care continues with reliable equipment.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Charging Accessory Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the dock has no indication, the device does not detect the dock, charging stops intermittently, or the power adapter does not energize the system. Test the complaint using the exact adapter, cord, dock, and device reported. Expected outcome: The failing part of the external charging path is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Wall Outlet
steps.instructions: Test the outlet according to facility electrical safety practices. Confirm switched or emergency-power receptacles are active and that the plug fits securely. Expected outcome: The outlet provides reliable power. If the accessory works on another verified outlet, refer the original receptacle for facilities correction.

steps.title: 4. Confirm the Correct Approved Power Adapter
steps.instructions: Compare the adapter identification with the equipment configuration and facility records. Do not use an adapter simply because its connector fits. Inspect the plug, cable, brick, strain reliefs, and connector for damage, heat, or discoloration. Expected outcome: The correct approved adapter is present and visibly safe.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Dock and Device Contacts
steps.instructions: Disconnect power before inspection. Check the charging dock and mating device surfaces for debris, dried residue, corrosion, moisture, recessed contacts, or physical damage. Clean external surfaces and contacts only through approved methods. Allow them to dry completely before reconnecting power. Expected outcome: Charging contacts are clean, dry, aligned, and undamaged.

steps.title: 6. Verify Correct Dock Positioning
steps.instructions: Place the device in the dock using its normal alignment and retention features. Confirm it sits fully without rocking, interference, or cable tension. Do not modify the dock, add spacers, or force the device into position. Expected outcome: The device seats consistently and displays the expected charging indication.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Cable Routing and Connector Retention
steps.instructions: Confirm the adapter cable is not sharply bent, trapped behind the cart, pulled sideways, or supporting the weight of the dock. Reseat the adapter connection at the dock and wall outlet. Expected outcome: All power connections remain secure during normal cart or device movement.

steps.title: 8. Substitute Known-Good External Power Components
steps.instructions: Use a known-good approved adapter with the suspect dock, then a known-good compatible dock with the original device. Change one item at a time. Expected outcome: The failure follows the adapter, dock, or device. Remove the identified defective accessory from service.

steps.title: 9. Test the Suspect Accessory With Another Compatible Device
steps.instructions: When available, test the dock or adapter with another verified compatible GlideScope component. Expected outcome: The comparison confirms whether the external charging accessory itself is defective.

steps.title: 10. Complete Final Charging Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm the device recognizes external power, begins charging, remains connected during normal movement, and shows an increasing battery state. Verify safe condition of all cords and connections. Perform electrical safety testing when required by facility policy or the repair performed. Expected outcome: Charging remains stable and repeatable. The dock or adapter may return to service only after all required checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GlideScope would not charge when placed in its dock.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried residue on the dock charging contacts that prevented consistent contact.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned and dried the external contacts according to approved procedures and verified stable charging with an increasing battery indication.

title: Verathon GlideScope Video Laryngoscope - Display Hinge, Mount, or Cart Connection Problem
description: Addresses unstable positioning caused by loose mounting, damaged hardware, cable strain, cart wear, obstruction, or mechanical connection failure.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Prevent Equipment Movement
steps.instructions: Do not use a GlideScope with a loose display, unstable cart, damaged hinge, or insecure mount during airway management. Move the patient to another verified system and stabilize the affected equipment. Disconnect power before moving a cart when cable damage or electrical strain is possible. Expected outcome: The patient is protected from falling equipment, sudden display movement, and interrupted visualization.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Mechanical Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether the display droops, will not rotate, moves too freely, binds, separates from the mount, vibrates during cart movement, or loses video when repositioned. Reproduce the condition without a patient and with the cart stationary. Expected outcome: The affected hinge, mount, cart joint, or cable-routing point is identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Immediate Structural Hazards
steps.instructions: Examine the display support, hinge, fasteners, cart pole, base, handle, shelves, casters, and mounting interface for cracks, bending, missing hardware, looseness, corrosion, or impact damage. Do not use the system if the display could fall or the cart could tip. Expected outcome: No unsafe structural condition is present. Any cracked, separated, or unstable assembly is removed from service immediately.

steps.title: 4. Verify Cart Stability and Caster Operation
steps.instructions: Place the cart on a level surface. Check that casters roll, swivel, and lock as intended and that the base sits evenly. Remove excess or unapproved accessories that may affect balance. Expected outcome: The cart remains stable when stationary and moves predictably when unlocked.

steps.title: 5. Check Mount Engagement
steps.instructions: Confirm the display or monitor is fully engaged with its approved mounting interface and any retention latch or locking feature is in the correct position. Do not add improvised hardware, tape, or unapproved fasteners. Expected outcome: The display is securely retained with no unintended separation or excessive play.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Accessible External Fasteners
steps.instructions: Check only user- or service-accessible external fasteners identified for routine inspection. Tighten them only when authorized and using the correct procedure and tools. Do not disassemble the hinge or internal mount mechanism without approved instructions. Expected outcome: Authorized external fasteners are secure. If this restores stable positioning, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 7. Check Hinge Movement and Holding Ability
steps.instructions: Move the display slowly through its normal adjustment range. Observe for binding, grinding, sudden release, inability to hold position, or excessive looseness. Keep hands clear of pinch points. Expected outcome: The display moves smoothly and remains in the selected position without drifting.

steps.title: 8. Inspect Cable Routing Through the Mount and Cart
steps.instructions: Confirm power, video, and accessory cables have adequate slack and are not wrapped around the hinge, pinched between mount surfaces, dragging beneath casters, or pulling the display out of position. Re-route cables through approved clips or guides. Expected outcome: Cables move freely without strain, pinching, or interference. If proper routing resolves the issue, complete final verification.

steps.title: 9. Check Whether Movement Affects Video or Power
steps.instructions: With the system operating on the bench, reposition the display and cart through normal movement. Observe for image interruption, connector movement, or power loss. Stop immediately if a cable or connector appears damaged. Expected outcome: Mechanical adjustment does not interrupt video or power. Any associated electrical intermittency is isolated and corrected before return to service.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Mechanical and Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm the display holds position, the mount remains secure, the cart rolls and locks normally, cables remain protected, and the system maintains stable power and video during normal repositioning. Complete required safety inspection after any mechanical repair. Expected outcome: The complete assembly is stable, secure, and functional. It may return to service only after all required checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GlideScope display slowly dropped downward after being positioned.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that an authorized external mount fastener had loosened, allowing excess movement.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the fastener using the approved procedure and verified that the display held position while video and power remained stable.

helpfulDetails: Effect of movement on video or power

title: Verathon GlideScope Video Laryngoscope - HDMI / External Video Output Failure
description: Addresses missing external video caused by display selection, cable, adapter, input, compatibility, resolution handling, or output hardware problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Primary Visualization
steps.instructions: Do not depend on an external display as the only airway image unless the complete video path has been verified. Maintain the GlideScope’s primary display and a backup airway method during troubleshooting. Do not adjust external video connections during an active airway procedure. Expected outcome: Primary airway visualization remains reliable while the external-output issue is evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact External-Output Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the external monitor shows no signal, intermittent video, distorted image, incorrect color, or delayed display. Ask whether the output previously worked with the same cable and receiving display. Reproduce the issue using the reported setup away from patient care. Expected outcome: The failure is defined and the involved source, cable, adapter, and receiving display are identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify the GlideScope Primary Image
steps.instructions: Confirm the GlideScope monitor displays a stable live image. External output cannot be evaluated accurately if the source image is already failing. Expected outcome: The primary display shows normal live video. If not, troubleshoot the source image first.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Receiving Display and Input Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm the external monitor or recorder is powered and set to the correct HDMI or video input. Test its input using another known-good approved source when permitted. Expected outcome: The receiving device and selected input are functional.

steps.title: 5. Inspect and Reseat the Video Cable
steps.instructions: Disconnect and inspect the HDMI or approved external-video cable for bent contacts, damaged connector shells, pinching, loose strain reliefs, or contamination. Reconnect both ends fully. Avoid side-loading the connectors. Expected outcome: The cable is intact and securely seated. If the external image appears and remains stable, complete final verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Any Approved Adapter or Interface
steps.instructions: If the installation uses an approved adapter, converter, wall plate, cart interface, or distribution device, verify power, seating, and correct signal path. Bypass optional infrastructure with a direct approved connection when practical and authorized. Expected outcome: The external image works through a direct connection or the failed intermediate interface is identified.

steps.title: 7. Test With a Known-Good Approved Cable
steps.instructions: Replace the suspect cable with a known-good cable of the correct type and suitable length. Expected outcome: A stable image with the known-good cable identifies the original cable as defective.

steps.title: 8. Test Another Verified External Display
steps.instructions: Connect the GlideScope output directly to another verified compatible display or recorder when available. Expected outcome: The result determines whether the failure is associated with the GlideScope output or the original receiving device.

steps.title: 9. Check User-Accessible Output Settings
steps.instructions: Review normal user-accessible settings related to external display output. Compare with another identical working system when available. Do not enter restricted service menus or make unauthorized resolution, firmware, or configuration changes. Expected outcome: External output is enabled and set appropriately for the supported configuration.

steps.title: 10. Perform Complete Video-Path Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm live video appears simultaneously where expected, remains stable during normal cable movement, and maintains acceptable orientation, color, and timing. Verify the primary display continues to operate normally. Expected outcome: The full external-video path is stable and clinically usable. The system may return to service after required checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the external procedure monitor displayed “no signal” from the GlideScope.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the receiving monitor was set to a different HDMI input than the connected GlideScope cable.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering selected the correct input and verified a stable external image while the primary GlideScope display remained normal.

helpfulDetails: No signal, intermittent, distorted, or delayed output

title: Verathon GlideScope Video Laryngoscope - Image Color, Brightness, or White Balance Abnormal
description: Addresses abnormal image appearance caused by contamination, lighting, settings, cable problems, display adjustment, or imaging-component failure.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Confirm Adequate Visualization
steps.instructions: Do not use the GlideScope if abnormal color, brightness, or contrast prevents reliable airway landmark identification. Provide another verified visualization method before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Airway care continues with a clear and dependable image.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Image Abnormality
steps.instructions: Determine whether the image is too dark, washed out, unusually tinted, low contrast, oversaturated, or inconsistent as the device moves. Ask whether menus and text also appear abnormal. Reproduce the complaint using a neutral nonpatient test scene under normal room lighting. Expected outcome: The problem is separated into live-camera image, entire display, or environmental appearance.

steps.title: 3. Inspect and Clean the Camera Window
steps.instructions: Check the optical window for residue, staining, moisture, haze, scratches, or dried disinfectant. Clean and dry it using approved methods. Expected outcome: The optical window is clear and unobstructed. If normal color and brightness return, complete final verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Check Ambient Lighting and Reflections
steps.instructions: Test away from direct procedure lights, sunlight, colored surfaces, and strong reflections. Aim the camera at a neutral surface under ordinary room lighting. Expected outcome: The image appears consistent in a controlled environment. A problem caused only by unusual lighting is distinguished from device failure.

steps.title: 5. Verify Display Brightness and User Settings
steps.instructions: Review normal user-accessible display and image settings. Confirm brightness is not at an extreme and that an unintended user profile or display mode is not active. Do not enter restricted service menus or change calibration values. Expected outcome: User-accessible settings are appropriate and produce a usable image.

steps.title: 6. Compare Menus With the Live Image
steps.instructions: Observe whether menu text, icons, and backgrounds have normal color and brightness. If menus appear normal while the live image is abnormal, focus on the camera, baton, handle, or video cable. If the entire screen is abnormal, the monitor display path may be involved. Expected outcome: The issue is isolated to the camera image or the complete display.

steps.title: 7. Inspect and Reseat the Video Connections
steps.instructions: Power down when appropriate. Inspect the imaging component and video cable connectors for contamination, moisture, damage, or incomplete seating. Reconnect them securely. Expected outcome: All connections are clean, dry, and fully seated. If image appearance returns to normal, complete final testing.

steps.title: 8. Substitute a Known-Good Imaging Component or Cable
steps.instructions: Test with a known-good approved camera, video baton, handle, or cable one item at a time. Expected outcome: The abnormal image follows one external component or remains with the monitor.

steps.title: 9. Compare With Another Verified Monitor
steps.instructions: Connect the suspect imaging component to another compatible verified GlideScope monitor when available, or connect a known-good component to the suspect monitor. Expected outcome: The comparison distinguishes an imaging-component problem from a display or monitor problem.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Image Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm normal color, brightness, contrast, orientation, and stability under ordinary room and procedure lighting. Verify display adjustment controls and normal movement. Expected outcome: The image remains clear and clinically usable. The system may return to service only after all required checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GlideScope live image appeared unusually blue and dim.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found moisture and cleaning residue on the external camera window.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned and fully dried the optical surface and verified normal image color, brightness, and stability.

helpfulDetails: Dark, washed out, tinted, or low-contrast image

title: Verathon GlideScope Video Laryngoscope - Image Cuts In and Out During Use
description: Addresses intermittent image loss caused by power instability, loose connections, damaged cables, component movement, contamination, or system faults.

steps.title: 1. Stop Clinical Use and Maintain Airway Visualization
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot image loss while the device is supporting an airway procedure. Change immediately to another verified visualization method and maintain appropriate backup airway equipment. Remove the GlideScope system from the active procedure area if the image cannot be trusted. Expected outcome: Airway management continues without dependence on an unreliable image.

steps.title: 2. Clarify the Reported Image Behavior
steps.instructions: Determine whether the display goes completely black, freezes on the last frame, flickers, shows interference, or restarts. Ask whether the failure occurs with movement, on battery power, on AC power, or after a period of use. Reproduce the issue on the bench using the reported configuration when safe. Expected outcome: The exact symptom and triggering condition are documented. If the image remains stable through repeated testing, continue inspection before release.

steps.title: 3. Confirm Monitor Power Remains Stable
steps.instructions: Observe whether power indicators, screen backlighting, and startup status change when the image disappears. Test using the approved AC source and a sufficiently charged battery when applicable. Verify the power adapter and charging connection are secure. Expected outcome: The monitor remains powered while only the live image is interrupted. If the monitor itself loses power, troubleshoot the power system instead.

steps.title: 4. Reseat the Imaging Connections
steps.instructions: Power down when appropriate. Disconnect and inspect the camera, baton, handle, and video cable connectors. Remove external debris according to approved cleaning practices and allow all connections to dry fully. Reconnect each component firmly without forcing it. Expected outcome: All connections are clean, dry, and fully seated. If image loss no longer occurs, perform final verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Cable During Normal Movement
steps.instructions: Examine the cable and strain reliefs for pinching, cuts, tight bends, or looseness. With a live test image, gently move the cable through the same normal range used clinically. Do not flex damaged areas aggressively or continue testing if conductors may be exposed. Expected outcome: Normal cable movement does not interrupt the image. If movement causes failure, remove the cable or affected component from service.

steps.title: 6. Verify Secure Imaging-Component Attachment
steps.instructions: Confirm the video baton, camera, or handle is assembled and seated correctly with any compatible blade, sleeve, or accessory used by the system. Check that accessory positioning is not pulling on the imaging component or partially disengaging a connector. Expected outcome: The imaging component remains mechanically secure throughout normal positioning.

steps.title: 7. Clean and Inspect the Camera Window
steps.instructions: Inspect the camera window for residue, moisture, scratches, or contamination that could be interpreted as intermittent image loss. Clean and disinfect only according to approved procedures. Allow the component to dry completely before retesting. Expected outcome: The camera window is clean and clear. If image quality remains continuous after cleaning, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 8. Substitute Known-Good External Components
steps.instructions: Test with a known-good approved video cable and then a known-good compatible camera, baton, or handle. Change only one component at a time. Expected outcome: The issue follows one interchangeable external component or remains with the monitor. Remove any identified defective accessory from service.

steps.title: 9. Check for Environmental Interference or Overheating
steps.instructions: Ensure ventilation openings are unobstructed and the system is not exposed to excessive heat, direct fluid spray, or cable routing near equipment that visibly disrupts the image. Do not assume electromagnetic interference without confirming that the symptom changes when the system is relocated or nearby equipment is removed from the test setup. Expected outcome: The image remains stable in an appropriate operating environment.

steps.title: 10. Complete Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Operate the system long enough to cover the reported failure period. Verify startup, component recognition, continuous live video, image clarity, normal movement, battery and AC operation as applicable, and secure cart placement. Expected outcome: The image remains continuous throughout repeated testing. The device may return to service after all required checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GlideScope image repeatedly went blank when the handle was repositioned.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the video cable connector was partially seated at the monitor.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated and secured the connector, then verified continuous live video during repeated handle and cable movement.

helpfulDetails: Black, frozen, flickering, or distorted image

title: Verathon GlideScope Video Laryngoscope - Screen Brightness or Display Settings Will Not Adjust
description: Addresses unresponsive display adjustment caused by locked controls, touchscreen or key problems, software state, configuration, or display failure.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Confirm Display Usability
steps.instructions: Do not use the GlideScope for airway management if the display cannot be viewed adequately in the clinical environment. Provide another verified visualization device before troubleshooting. If the screen is excessively dark, unstable, or unreadable, remove the system from active use. Expected outcome: Patient care continues with a clearly visible, reliable display.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Adjustment Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether brightness cannot be increased, cannot be decreased, returns to a previous level, or whether all display controls are unresponsive. Ask whether the issue affects touchscreen controls, physical keys, or both. Reproduce the complaint away from patient care. Expected outcome: The affected control and display behavior are identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Normal Startup and System Responsiveness
steps.instructions: Power-cycle the monitor using the normal operator control. Confirm it reaches the standard operating screen and that other menus or functions respond. Do not repeatedly interrupt startup if the unit is in a boot loop or update state. Expected outcome: The system starts normally and responds to basic controls. If the entire system is frozen, follow software-freeze troubleshooting instead.

steps.title: 4. Clean and Inspect the Touchscreen or Keys
steps.instructions: Check for gloves, moisture, disinfectant residue, protective film, labels, or physical obstruction affecting the controls. Clean and dry the external control surfaces using approved methods. Inspect buttons for sticking, damage, or incomplete travel. Expected outcome: Controls are clean, dry, and mechanically unobstructed.

steps.title: 5. Confirm the Correct Adjustment Method
steps.instructions: Navigate through the normal user-accessible display controls for the specific GlideScope configuration. Verify that the technician is adjusting brightness rather than another image parameter. Do not enter unauthorized service menus or change restricted configuration settings. Expected outcome: The correct control is selected and the displayed setting changes normally. If adjustment is restored, complete final verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 6. Check for Control Lock or Restricted Profile
steps.instructions: Determine whether a user-accessible lock, clinical profile, or facility configuration limits display changes. Compare with another identical verified system if available. Do not bypass passwords or alter protected settings without authorization. Expected outcome: Any authorized control restriction is identified and corrected through the approved process.

steps.title: 7. Test Under Different Ambient Lighting
steps.instructions: Move the monitor away from direct overhead lighting, sunlight, or strong reflections. Confirm that apparent brightness problems are not caused by glare or viewing angle. Adjust the monitor position and cart height as appropriate. Expected outcome: The screen remains readable in a normal clinical environment.

steps.title: 8. Compare Touchscreen and Physical Controls
steps.instructions: If the system provides more than one user input method, test each approved method. Determine whether only one control path fails. Expected outcome: The issue is isolated to the touchscreen, a physical control, or the display-setting function itself.

steps.title: 9. Compare With a Known-Good System
steps.instructions: Use another verified GlideScope of the same configuration to compare menu behavior, available settings, and visible brightness range. Do not copy configuration files or settings unless authorized. Expected outcome: The suspect unit’s behavior is confirmed as abnormal rather than a normal model limitation.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify the setting changes through its available range, remains at the selected level after normal navigation or restart when designed to do so, and leaves the live image and menus clearly visible. Check other basic controls and live video before return to service. Expected outcome: Brightness and display settings respond reliably. The system may return to service after all required checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GlideScope screen brightness would not increase using the touchscreen control.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried disinfectant residue on the touchscreen that prevented reliable input.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned and dried the touchscreen according to approved procedures and verified repeated brightness adjustment and a clear live image.

title: Verathon GlideScope Video Laryngoscope - Startup Failure, Boot Loop, or Software Freeze
description: Addresses failed startup or freezing caused by power, battery, connected accessories, storage media, software state, or internal system faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove the System From Airway Use
steps.instructions: Do not use a GlideScope that fails to start, repeatedly restarts, or freezes. Move the patient to another verified airway visualization device and maintain an appropriate backup method. Disconnect the system immediately if there is unusual heat, odor, liquid intrusion, or electrical damage. Expected outcome: Patient care continues with reliable equipment, and the unstable system is isolated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup Behavior
steps.instructions: Determine whether the screen remains blank, stops at a logo, repeatedly restarts, freezes after reaching the operating screen, or responds slowly. Record any displayed message exactly. Ask whether the problem began after charging, transport, cleaning, accessory connection, storage insertion, or a software update. Expected outcome: The startup stage and triggering condition are documented.

steps.title: 3. Verify the AC Power Source
steps.instructions: Test the outlet according to facility policy and confirm the approved power adapter is fully connected. Inspect the cord, adapter, and plug for damage or overheating. Attempt one normal startup on a verified AC source. Expected outcome: The system receives stable approved external power. If it starts normally, continue battery and functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Check Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Observe the battery indicator when available. A deeply discharged or failed battery may prevent reliable startup even when external power is connected in some configurations. Allow charging according to approved instructions before one additional startup attempt. Expected outcome: The device has sufficient power for a controlled startup test.

steps.title: 5. Disconnect Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: Power down when possible. Remove approved removable media, external video cables, barcode devices, network cables, and other nonessential accessories. Leave only the components required for basic startup. Do not disconnect permanently installed internal assemblies. Expected outcome: The system starts with a minimal external configuration. Reconnect accessories one at a time to identify the trigger.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Imaging and Power Connections
steps.instructions: Check the camera, baton, handle, video cable, charger, and dock connections for partial seating, contamination, moisture, or damage. Disconnect any visibly damaged accessory before restarting. Expected outcome: External connections are clean, dry, and secure, and no damaged accessory remains attached.

steps.title: 7. Perform One Controlled Power Reset
steps.instructions: With the system removed from clinical use, follow the normal user-accessible shutdown and restart method. If the device is frozen and the applicable manufacturer instructions permit a power reset, perform it once. Do not repeatedly force shutdowns, interrupt an update, or use undocumented key combinations. Expected outcome: The system completes startup and remains responsive. If so, continue extended functional testing before return to service.

steps.title: 8. Check Removable Storage or Connected Media
steps.instructions: If the system starts without removable media but freezes when media is installed, inspect the media for damage, incompatibility, or corruption. Test with known-good approved media when applicable. Protect all stored patient information. Expected outcome: The system remains stable with approved functional media, or the suspect media is isolated.

steps.title: 9. Observe the System Through an Extended Test
steps.instructions: Allow the monitor to remain powered through the period when the freeze usually occurs. Test normal user-accessible menus, live video, controls, recording functions if applicable, and AC-to-battery transition. Expected outcome: The system remains responsive without restarting or freezing.

steps.title: 10. Complete Final Verification or Escalate
steps.instructions: Repeat startup several times using the normal process. Confirm reliable boot completion, control response, component recognition, live image, power operation, and no recurring software freeze. Expected outcome: The system starts and operates consistently. If any boot loop or freeze returns, remove it from service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GlideScope repeatedly restarted at the startup screen.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that damaged removable storage media caused the system to restart when installed.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed the damaged media, installed approved known-good media, and verified repeated normal startup and stable live video.

helpfulDetails: Blank screen, logo freeze, boot loop, or operating freeze

title: Verathon GlideScope Video Laryngoscope - Video Baton, Camera, or Handle Not Recognized
description: Addresses an unrecognized imaging component caused by connection, compatibility, contamination, cable, power, or configuration problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Airway Readiness
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable video laryngoscope while it is being used for airway management. Transfer immediately to another verified airway device and ensure an appropriate backup airway method is available. Inspect the GlideScope system for impact damage, exposed conductors, liquid intrusion, unusual heat, odor, or visibly damaged connectors. Remove the equipment from service immediately if any unsafe condition is found. Expected outcome: The patient is supported with reliable airway equipment, and the GlideScope system is safe to evaluate.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Recognition Failure
steps.instructions: Ask clinical staff which video baton, camera, or handle was connected, whether the failure occurred at startup or during use, and whether any message or blank-image condition appeared. Reproduce the complaint away from patient care using the same monitor, imaging component, cable, and accessories when safe. Expected outcome: The affected component and exact failure condition are identified. If the system now recognizes the component consistently, complete functional verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 3. Verify Monitor Power and Normal Startup
steps.instructions: Confirm the monitor powers on normally and reaches its standard operating screen without freezing, restarting, or displaying unrelated power problems. If available, verify operation on both approved AC power and a sufficiently charged battery. Expected outcome: The monitor starts normally and remains stable. If monitor power is unreliable, address the power issue before continuing recognition troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Reseat All External Connections
steps.instructions: Power down the system when appropriate. Disconnect the video baton, camera, or handle and any intermediate video cable. Inspect each connector for incomplete seating, bent contacts, debris, moisture, corrosion, or damaged alignment features. Reconnect each component fully without forcing the connector. Confirm any locking or retention feature engages normally. Expected outcome: All connections are clean, dry, undamaged, and fully seated. If recognition returns and remains stable after repeated reconnection, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 5. Confirm Component Compatibility
steps.instructions: Verify that the connected video baton, camera, handle, cable, and monitor are approved for use together within the specific GlideScope configuration. Compare model labels, connector types, and facility inventory records. Do not force physically similar components together or change restricted configuration settings. Expected outcome: All connected components are confirmed compatible. An incompatible component is replaced with the correct approved component.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Imaging Component and Cable
steps.instructions: Examine the video baton, camera, or handle for cracks, damaged strain reliefs, contamination, loose housings, or evidence of fluid entry. Inspect the full cable length for cuts, kinks, compression, or intermittent movement at either end. Do not use a component that cannot be cleaned, disinfected, or safely connected according to facility and manufacturer requirements. Expected outcome: The component and cable show no visible defect. Any damaged item is removed from service.

steps.title: 7. Test With a Known-Good Compatible Component
steps.instructions: Connect a known-good compatible video baton, camera, handle, or cable one item at a time. Keep the original monitor and remaining accessories unchanged so the result isolates the affected part of the external system. Do not substitute unapproved accessories. Expected outcome: The known-good component is recognized consistently. If it is, remove the original component from service and complete final verification with the replacement.

steps.title: 8. Compare the Suspect Component on Another Compatible System
steps.instructions: When available, connect the suspect component to another verified compatible GlideScope monitor. Follow infection prevention requirements before transferring reusable airway components between systems. Expected outcome: The comparison determines whether the issue follows the imaging component or remains with the original monitor. Stop troubleshooting once the defective external component is isolated and removed from use.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Reconnect the verified components and power-cycle the system. Confirm recognition at startup, stable live video, proper orientation, acceptable image quality, and reliable operation while gently moving the external cable within normal handling limits. Perform any required post-service inspection or electrical safety testing appropriate to the work performed. Expected outcome: The system recognizes the imaging component repeatedly and maintains a stable image. The device may be returned to service only after all required checks pass.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Recognition Failure
steps.instructions: If compatible known-good external components are still not recognized, discontinue external troubleshooting. Do not enter unauthorized service modes, open sealed assemblies, or attempt board-level repair. Expected outcome: The system is removed from clinical use and routed for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GlideScope monitor did not recognize the connected video baton during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the video cable connector was not fully seated and had visible debris around the connector interface.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned the external connector area, reconnected the cable securely, and verified repeated component recognition with a stable live image.

helpfulDetails: Whether the issue followed the component

title: Verathon GlideScope Video Laryngoscope - Video Cable or Connector Intermittent
description: Addresses intermittent video operation caused by loose seating, connector contamination, strain, cable damage, or incompatible accessories.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove Unreliable Equipment
steps.instructions: Do not continue using a GlideScope system with an intermittent video connection during airway management. Move immediately to another verified airway device and maintain an appropriate backup airway method. Inspect for exposed conductors, cracked connectors, liquid intrusion, unusual heat, or severe cable damage. Remove the system from service immediately if any unsafe condition is present. Expected outcome: Patient care continues with reliable equipment, and the affected system is isolated for safe evaluation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm How the Intermittency Occurs
steps.instructions: Ask whether the image fails when the cable is moved, when the handle is repositioned, after startup, or without physical movement. Determine whether the image becomes blank, distorted, frozen, or temporarily disconnected. Reproduce the symptom away from patient care using normal handling only. Do not sharply bend or intentionally stress the cable. Expected outcome: The movement, position, or condition associated with the failure is identified. If the connection remains stable and the complaint cannot be reproduced, continue inspection before returning the device to service.

steps.title: 3. Verify Stable Monitor Power
steps.instructions: Confirm the monitor remains powered and does not restart when the image drops out. Check the approved power adapter, charging connection, battery status, and power cord as applicable. A monitor power interruption can resemble a video cable failure. Expected outcome: Monitor power remains stable while the video symptom occurs. Any power-related problem is corrected before continuing.

steps.title: 4. Inspect and Reseat the Cable Connections
steps.instructions: Power down when appropriate. Disconnect both ends of the video cable and inspect for debris, moisture, corrosion, bent contacts, damaged alignment features, or loose connector shells. Reconnect each end fully and confirm any locking or retention mechanism engages normally. Do not force a connector. Expected outcome: Both connectors are clean, dry, undamaged, and securely seated. If the image remains stable after repeated reconnection, complete final verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Full Cable and Strain Reliefs
steps.instructions: Examine the entire cable under good lighting. Pay particular attention to areas near strain reliefs, cart routing points, bends, clamps, and locations where the cable may have been pinched or rolled over. Do not tape, splice, or field-repair a damaged medical video cable. Expected outcome: The cable has no cuts, flattened sections, sharp kinks, looseness, or exposed shielding. A damaged cable is removed from service.

steps.title: 6. Check Cable Routing and Mechanical Strain
steps.instructions: Confirm the cable has adequate slack during normal use and is not supporting the weight of the handle, camera, or monitor. Verify it is not tightly wrapped around the cart, trapped beneath equipment, or pulled sideways at the connector. Reposition the cable to maintain a natural bend radius without tension. Expected outcome: The cable remains stable without connector strain. If proper routing eliminates the interruption, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 7. Test With a Known-Good Compatible Cable
steps.instructions: Install a known-good approved video cable while keeping the same monitor and imaging component. Operate the system and gently reposition the cable within normal clinical movement. Expected outcome: A stable image with the known-good cable identifies the original cable as defective. Remove the suspect cable from service.

steps.title: 8. Test the Imaging Component Separately
steps.instructions: If the symptom remains with a known-good cable, test the camera, video baton, or handle with another verified compatible system when available. Follow all required cleaning and disinfection procedures before exchanging reusable airway components. Expected outcome: The comparison determines whether the intermittency follows the imaging component or remains with the original monitor connection.

steps.title: 9. Verify the Monitor-Side Connection
steps.instructions: With a known-good cable and imaging component connected, observe whether light normal contact near the monitor connector causes loss of image. Do not apply excessive force. A loose, recessed, or visibly damaged monitor connector requires service-level evaluation. Expected outcome: The monitor-side connection remains stable during normal handling. If it does not, remove the monitor from service.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Power-cycle the system several times and confirm reliable component recognition, continuous live video, acceptable image quality, and stable operation throughout normal cable movement and cart positioning. Complete any required post-service safety testing. Expected outcome: The image remains continuous with no flicker, blanking, or disconnect indications. The system may return to service only after all required checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GlideScope image disappeared whenever the video cable was moved.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a damaged strain relief at the imaging-component end of the video cable.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the cable with an approved compatible cable and verified a continuous image during repeated normal movement.

helpfulDetails: Position or movement that triggered failure
Blank, frozen, flickering, or distorted image

title: Verathon GlideScope Video Laryngoscope - Video Recording or Snapshot Capture Failure
description: Addresses failed recording or image capture caused by storage, media, controls, permissions, capacity, configuration, or software problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve Airway Priorities
steps.instructions: Recording and snapshot functions are secondary to airway visualization. Do not interrupt airway management or manipulate a malfunctioning system while it is being used on a patient. Continue clinical care with a stable live image or move to another verified device if primary visualization is affected. Expected outcome: Patient safety and live airway visualization are maintained independently of recording functions.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Capture Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether recording will not start, stops unexpectedly, snapshots are not saved, files cannot be found, or capture controls do not respond. Record any displayed message exactly. Reproduce the issue using nonpatient test content and the same storage configuration. Expected outcome: The failure is identified as control, storage, file-retrieval, or software related.

steps.title: 3. Verify Live Video and Basic System Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm the camera is recognized and a stable live image is present. Verify the monitor is not frozen and other user controls respond normally. Recording troubleshooting should not proceed until basic video operation is stable. Expected outcome: Live video and general system controls operate normally.

steps.title: 4. Confirm the Correct Capture Control
steps.instructions: Use the normal user-accessible recording or snapshot control for the specific GlideScope configuration. Check whether the control is on the monitor, handle, touchscreen, or accessory. Inspect the button or touchscreen area for damage, contamination, or obstruction. Expected outcome: The correct capture control is used and responds normally.

steps.title: 5. Check Storage Presence and Capacity
steps.instructions: Verify that the required approved storage location or removable media is present, correctly inserted, and recognized. Review available storage through normal user-accessible menus. Do not delete patient data without authorization and an approved data-handling process. Expected outcome: Sufficient recognized storage is available. If storage is full, authorized data management restores capture function.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Removable Media When Applicable
steps.instructions: Confirm removable media is the approved type and is not physically damaged, write-protected, contaminated, or improperly seated. Do not use unknown media that could introduce malware or corrupt files. Expected outcome: Approved media is fully inserted and available for writing.

steps.title: 7. Test With Known-Good Approved Media
steps.instructions: When applicable, use known-good approved media with no protected patient information. Attempt a test snapshot and short recording. Expected outcome: Successful capture with known-good media identifies the original media as defective, incompatible, full, or write-protected.

steps.title: 8. Verify Date, Time, and File Retrieval Location
steps.instructions: Confirm the system date and time are reasonable and that staff are looking in the correct folder, patient record, or media location. An incorrectly dated file may appear missing. Do not change network or protected configuration without authorization. Expected outcome: Newly captured test files appear in the expected location with identifiable timestamps.

steps.title: 9. Restart the System Normally
steps.instructions: After confirming no active clinical use or file-writing process, perform a normal shutdown and restart. Reattempt capture with a stable live image and approved storage. Do not repeatedly power-cycle a unit that freezes or restarts during boot. Expected outcome: Recording and snapshot functions return after a normal restart. If so, complete repeated verification before return to service.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Capture a test snapshot and recording, stop the recording normally, locate the saved files, and confirm they can be opened or exported through the approved workflow. Ensure no test content is mistaken for a patient record. Expected outcome: Capture, storage, retrieval, and playback or review work consistently. The system may return to service after all required checks pass.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the GlideScope snapshot button responded but no image file appeared in storage.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the approved removable storage media was full.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering followed the authorized data-management process, installed available approved media, and verified successful snapshot capture and retrieval.

title: Verathon Prime Plus Bladder Scanner - Barcode Scanner or Patient ID Entry Failure
description: Helps isolate barcode quality, scanner positioning, connection, patient-entry workflow, control-input, and configuration causes of patient identification failure.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Identification and Confirm the Complaint
steps.instructions: Do not allow incorrect patient identification to be attached to an examination. If barcode entry is unreliable, use the facility-approved manual patient-identification process or another verified scanner. Confirm whether: Barcode scanner does not activate Barcode is read but incorrect data appears Some barcodes work and others do not Manual patient ID entry also fails Patient fields cannot be selected or edited Expected outcome: The exact identification failure is defined without risking assignment of data to the wrong patient.

steps.title: 2. Inspect the Barcode
steps.instructions: Check the test barcode or patient wristband for: Damage Wrinkles Smearing Poor printing Reflective covering Curvature Obstruction Use an approved test barcode when available rather than repeatedly scanning a patient's wristband during troubleshooting. Expected outcome: A clean, readable barcode is available for testing. If replacing a damaged label restores reliable scanning, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 3. Verify Scanner Positioning
steps.instructions: Attempt scanning at a normal working distance and angle. Avoid holding the scanner excessively close, far away, or at an extreme angle. Ensure the barcode is adequately illuminated and unobstructed. Expected outcome: The scanner recognizes the barcode consistently. If positioning corrects the issue, verify repeated successful scans and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Barcode Scanner and Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect the barcode scanner housing, cable, accessible connector, or integrated scanning area as applicable for: Physical damage Loose connection Contamination Cracked lens or window Cable strain Reseat accessible connections if appropriate. Expected outcome: The barcode scanner is physically intact and securely connected. If reseating restores operation, verify repeated scans.

steps.title: 5. Compare With a Known-Good Barcode
steps.instructions: Scan a known-good barcode that is compatible with the facility's normal workflow. This helps distinguish a scanner problem from a single poor-quality barcode. Expected outcome: The known-good barcode scans successfully. If only the original barcode fails, the scanner is functioning and the label or source data should be addressed.

steps.title: 6. Test Manual Patient ID Entry
steps.instructions: Using an approved test workflow, determine whether patient ID can be entered manually through the normal operator-accessible controls. Do not use real patient identifiers for unnecessary testing. Expected outcome: Manual entry is accepted and displayed correctly. If manual entry also fails, the problem may involve the user interface, application, or configuration rather than the barcode reader alone.

steps.title: 7. Verify Authorized Workflow and Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm the normal patient-identification workflow is selected and that barcode use has not been unintentionally bypassed or changed within authorized operator-accessible settings. Do not enter restricted service menus or alter institutional interface configuration without authorization. Expected outcome: The scanner is using the approved identification workflow. If an authorized workflow correction restores scanning, document the change and proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Using approved test data, confirm: Barcode scanner activates Barcode is read consistently Correct identifier populates the intended field Manual entry works if supported by workflow A representative exam can be associated with the correct test record Expected outcome: Patient identification functions reliably and accurately. Troubleshooting can stop and the device may return to service.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported the Prime Plus would not read patient wristband barcodes but manual patient ID entry still worked.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the barcode scanner connection was loose at the accessible external connector.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated the connection, verified repeated reads with an approved test barcode, confirmed correct field population, and returned the scanner to service.

title: Verathon Prime Plus Bladder Scanner - Battery Will Not Charge or Runtime Is Short
description: Helps isolate charging, power-source, battery-contact, docking, and usage-related causes of poor charging or unexpectedly short battery runtime.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care and Confirm the Complaint
steps.instructions: Remove the Prime Plus from active clinical use if battery performance is unreliable enough that the scanner may shut down during an examination. Provide staff with another verified bladder scanner if needed. Confirm whether the complaint is: Battery will not charge Charge indication is absent or abnormal Unit operates only while connected to external power Battery runtime is noticeably shorter than expected Unit shuts down unexpectedly Expected outcome: The exact battery or charging symptom is reproduced or clearly documented. If the complaint cannot be reproduced and normal operation is verified, troubleshooting can stop after appropriate functional verification.

steps.title: 2. Inspect the Scanner and Charging Equipment
steps.instructions: Inspect the scanner, power supply, charging cable, docking components, and accessible connectors for: Physical damage Bent or contaminated contacts Loose connections Fluid intrusion Excessive heat Burn marks or odor Do not continue operating equipment showing evidence of overheating, electrical damage, or liquid intrusion. Expected outcome: Charging components are clean, undamaged, and securely connected. If damaged components are found, remove the device from service until corrected.

steps.title: 3. Verify the AC Power Source
steps.instructions: Confirm the charging power supply is connected correctly and test the receptacle with an appropriate outlet tester or known-good device when permitted by facility procedure. Try a different verified receptacle if necessary. Expected outcome: Reliable AC power is available to the charging system. If changing the outlet restores charging, the scanner issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop after verifying continued charging.

steps.title: 4. Verify the External Power Supply and Connections
steps.instructions: Reseat all accessible charging connections. Confirm the correct approved power supply and charging arrangement are being used. If another compatible, approved charging supply or dock is available, use a known-good substitution to isolate the scanner from the external charging equipment. Expected outcome: The scanner shows normal charging behavior with the verified charging equipment. If a known-good external component corrects the problem, replace or route the faulty accessory for repair and stop troubleshooting after verification.

steps.title: 5. Check Charging Position and Docking Contact
steps.instructions: If charging involves a dock or cradle, confirm the scanner is fully seated and the charging contacts align without requiring pressure, twisting, or repeated repositioning. Clean accessible contacts only according to approved facility or manufacturer cleaning practices. Expected outcome: The scanner maintains a stable charging indication when properly positioned. If reseating or cleaning the external contact area restores normal charging, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 6. Compare Battery Operation After Charging
steps.instructions: Allow the unit to charge normally, then operate it on battery while observing for: Unexpected shutdown Rapid decrease in displayed charge Intermittent power Battery-related warnings Excessive heating Do not intentionally run a questionable battery to failure during clinical use. Expected outcome: The scanner operates normally from battery without unexpected shutdown or abnormal charge behavior. If normal battery performance is restored, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm the scanner: Powers on normally Completes normal startup Operates from battery Accepts charging Performs a representative bladder scan Shuts down and restarts normally Expected outcome: Normal charging and battery-powered operation are verified. The device may be returned to service according to facility procedure.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported the Verathon Prime Plus would not remain charged and shut down shortly after being removed from its charger.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the charging connection was not making reliable contact because the scanner was not consistently seating in the charging position.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated and inspected the charging interface, verified stable charging, completed a representative scan on battery power, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether unit operated on external power
Charging indication before and after correction

title: Verathon Prime Plus Bladder Scanner - Calibration, Self-Test, or Startup Check Failure
description: Helps isolate power, probe, accessory, connection, environmental, startup, and authorized calibration-related causes when required checks do not complete successfully.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care and Remove an Unverified Unit From Use
steps.instructions: Do not use the Prime Plus for patient assessment when a required startup, self-test, or calibration-related check has failed and measurement reliability cannot be confirmed. Provide another verified bladder scanner. Record the exact displayed message or observed behavior. Expected outcome: The affected unit is removed from clinical dependency and the exact reported failure is documented.

steps.title: 2. Restart the Scanner Under Normal Conditions
steps.instructions: Power the device down using the normal procedure. Allow the shutdown to complete, then restart it without repeatedly cycling power. Observe the complete startup sequence. Expected outcome: The scanner completes startup normally. If the failure was transient and a representative functional test is also successful, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 3. Verify Power Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm the scanner has adequate power for testing. If battery status is questionable, connect the approved external power or charging arrangement. Inspect the power supply and accessible connections for damage or looseness. Expected outcome: Stable power is available and the startup check is not being interrupted by low or intermittent power. If stable power resolves the failure, verify normal operation before return to service.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Probe and Accessories
steps.instructions: Inspect the probe, cable, accessible connectors, dock, and other required external accessories for: Physical damage Loose connection Contamination Moisture Improper seating Cable strain Do not use a damaged probe or connector. Expected outcome: Required external components are intact and correctly connected. If reseating an accessory allows the self-test or startup check to pass, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 5. Remove Unnecessary External Connections
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential external accessories or communication connections when permitted, then restart the scanner in its basic approved configuration. This can help identify whether an external accessory is interfering with startup. Expected outcome: The scanner completes startup in its basic configuration. If an optional external accessory causes the failure, remove or replace that accessory and verify the scanner again.

steps.title: 6. Check the Environment
steps.instructions: Confirm the device is not being tested immediately after: Significant temperature change Exposure to excessive moisture Fluid contamination Storage in an unsuitable environment Physical impact Allow the device to reach an appropriate normal-use environment when needed before retesting. Expected outcome: Environmental conditions are suitable for normal operation. If the startup check then completes successfully, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 7. Use Only Authorized Calibration or Verification Functions
steps.instructions: If the reported condition specifically involves calibration, follow the applicable Verathon service documentation and use only authorized test equipment and procedures available to qualified Clinical Engineering personnel. Do not guess at calibration values, enter undocumented service menus, or modify calibration constants simply to clear a failure. Expected outcome: The authorized calibration or verification process either completes successfully or confirms that service-level evaluation is required.

steps.title: 8. Check for Repeatability
steps.instructions: Restart and test the device again under the same verified conditions. A single successful startup is not sufficient if the original failure was intermittent. Expected outcome: Startup and required checks pass consistently. If failures recur, remove the unit from service and escalate.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Before return to service, confirm: Startup completes normally Required self-checks complete Probe is recognized No unresolved warning remains A representative bladder scan completes normally Device operation is stable through restart Use any additional return-to-service testing required by manufacturer documentation and facility policy. Expected outcome: The scanner demonstrates consistent normal operation and required verification has passed. The device may be returned to service.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported the Prime Plus stopped during startup and would not complete its normal startup check.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the probe connection was partially seated, preventing stable probe recognition during startup.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated and inspected the probe connection, verified repeated successful startups and representative scans, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Point in startup where failure occurred

title: Verathon Prime Plus Bladder Scanner - Exam Will Not Save, Recall, or Transfer
description: Helps isolate workflow, storage, patient-selection, connectivity, configuration, and external communication causes affecting exam saving, recall, or transfer.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care and Preserve Clinical Information
steps.instructions: Do not delay necessary patient assessment while troubleshooting data handling. If the scanner can measure correctly but cannot save or transfer results, ensure clinically necessary findings are documented through an approved alternate process. Avoid deleting existing exams or changing system configuration during initial troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely and important examination results are preserved through an approved workflow.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint involves: Exam will not save Previously saved exam cannot be recalled Exam appears saved but cannot be transferred Only certain exams are affected Transfer fails consistently or intermittently Record any displayed message exactly as shown without interpreting or inventing an error meaning. Expected outcome: The affected part of the data workflow is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Basic Scanner Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm the Prime Plus: Starts normally Accepts normal user input Performs a representative scan Displays the resulting examination data normally Expected outcome: Core scanning functions operate correctly. If the scanner is generally unstable, remove it from service and troubleshoot the broader system problem first.

steps.title: 4. Verify Patient and Exam Workflow
steps.instructions: Confirm the correct patient or exam context is selected and that required operator-accessible fields are completed according to facility workflow. Do not change protected system configuration or create test patient records in a production system unless allowed by facility procedure. Expected outcome: The exam is associated with the intended record and can be saved normally. If correcting an incomplete or incorrect workflow restores saving, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Check Available Storage and Existing Exam Behavior
steps.instructions: Using normal operator-accessible functions, determine whether other recent exams can be saved and recalled. Avoid deleting stored clinical data unless authorized. Expected outcome: Exam storage and recall operate consistently. If only one record is affected, document the isolated event and verify normal operation with an approved test record.

steps.title: 6. Verify External Communication Connections
steps.instructions: If transfer is affected, inspect applicable accessible communication connections such as: Network cable Docking connection Approved communication accessory Wireless connection status, if used Reseat external connections where appropriate. Expected outcome: The external communication path is physically connected and stable. If reseating restores transfer, confirm repeated successful transfer before stopping.

steps.title: 7. Verify Network or Communication Availability
steps.instructions: When the device depends on facility network services, determine whether other devices on the same workflow are also affected. Coordinate with IT or the appropriate infrastructure team when a network, interface, server, or destination system problem is suspected. Do not change IP settings, security settings, or protected network configuration without authorization. Expected outcome: The required infrastructure is available and the scanner has normal communication. If an infrastructure outage explains the complaint, document the cause and coordinate restoration rather than performing unnecessary device repair.

steps.title: 8. Verify Authorized Configuration
steps.instructions: Review only operator-accessible or authorized configuration needed to confirm that the intended destination or transfer method is selected. Do not enter restricted service menus or make undocumented configuration changes. Expected outcome: The approved transfer destination and normal workflow are selected. If an authorized configuration correction restores operation, document the exact change and verify transfer.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Using an approved test workflow, confirm: A representative exam can be created The exam saves It can be recalled Transfer completes when applicable The receiving destination receives the expected information Expected outcome: The full intended exam workflow succeeds from acquisition through storage, recall, and transfer. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported that Prime Plus exams were completing normally but would not transfer to the expected destination.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external network connection was loose and the scanner did not have a stable communication path.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated the network connection, verified successful saving and transfer of an approved test exam, and returned the scanner to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether save, recall, transfer, or multiple functions failed

title: Verathon Prime Plus Bladder Scanner - Printer Will Not Print, Feed Paper, or Produces Faint Output
description: Helps isolate paper-loading, consumable, cover, feed-path, print-setting, and external printer-related causes of failed or poor-quality printing.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care and Confirm the Complaint
steps.instructions: A printer problem usually does not prevent bladder volume measurement, but do not delay clinically necessary assessment while troubleshooting documentation output. Ensure results can be recorded through an approved alternate workflow if printing is unavailable. Confirm whether the printer: Does not respond Attempts to print but does not feed paper Feeds paper incorrectly Produces blank or faint output Produces incomplete or distorted output Expected outcome: The exact printer failure is identified and can be tested safely without interfering with patient care.

steps.title: 2. Verify Basic Scanner Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm the Prime Plus powers on normally, completes startup, and can perform or access an examination result. A general scanner power or software issue should be addressed before treating the complaint as an isolated printer problem. Expected outcome: The scanner operates normally aside from the printing complaint. If the entire unit is unstable, remove it from service and escalate.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Paper Supply
steps.instructions: Open the accessible printer compartment and inspect the paper for: Empty roll Incorrect installation Wrinkling Torn edges Contamination Binding Improper routing Use only the appropriate approved paper type. Expected outcome: Paper is present, correctly loaded, and moves freely through the accessible feed path. If correcting the paper installation restores printing, troubleshooting can stop after several successful test prints.

steps.title: 4. Verify Paper Orientation
