steps.instructions: If the printer uses thermal paper, verify the roll is oriented correctly so the printable surface contacts the print mechanism as intended. Incorrect paper orientation can result in apparently blank output despite normal paper feeding. Expected outcome: Printed information is visible and legible. If reversing or correctly installing the paper restores output, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Printer Cover and Feed Path
steps.instructions: Check that the printer cover closes and latches properly and that no torn paper or foreign material is visible in the accessible feed path. Do not insert tools deeply into the mechanism or disassemble the printer assembly. Expected outcome: The cover closes normally and the paper path is unobstructed. If removing an accessible obstruction restores normal feeding, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Try a Fresh Known-Good Paper Roll
steps.instructions: Install a fresh, approved roll when faint, inconsistent, or blank printing is reported. Old, contaminated, damaged, or incompatible thermal paper may produce poor output even when the printer is functioning. Expected outcome: Print quality becomes clear and consistent. If a fresh paper roll corrects the issue, document the consumable cause and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 7. Verify Printing From a Representative Exam
steps.instructions: Perform or retrieve a non-patient test result as permitted by facility procedure and initiate printing through the normal operator-accessible workflow. Observe whether the printer responds, feeds smoothly, and produces complete output. Expected outcome: The printer produces a complete, legible record without feed errors. If successful, the device may proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm: Scanner functions normally Paper feeds without slipping or jamming Printed information is legible Multiple prints are consistent Printer compartment remains securely closed Expected outcome: Reliable printing is verified. The device may be returned to service according to facility procedure.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported the Prime Plus printer advanced paper but produced blank printouts.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the thermal paper roll installed with the printable surface oriented incorrectly.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reinstalled the paper correctly, produced several clear test printouts, verified scanner operation, and returned the device to service.

helpfulDetails: Printer response when print was selected

title: Verathon Prime Plus Bladder Scanner - Probe Cable, Connector, or Docking Communication Is Intermittent
description: Helps isolate loose connections, damaged cables, contaminated contacts, positioning, strain, and accessory-related causes of intermittent probe or docking communication.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care and Confirm the Complaint
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot intermittent probe communication while staff are depending on the scanner for a patient assessment. Provide another verified bladder scanner when the intermittent condition could affect examination reliability. Determine whether communication fails: Continuously Only when the cable is moved At a particular connector When placing or removing the device from a dock During scanning After transport Expected outcome: The intermittent condition and circumstances that reproduce it are clearly identified.

steps.title: 2. Inspect the Probe and Cable Externally
steps.instructions: Inspect the full accessible cable length and probe assembly for: Cuts Kinks Crushing Fraying Fluid intrusion Strain near cable exits Cracked housings Evidence of improper cleaning or impact Do not continue using a damaged patient-contact probe or cable. Expected outcome: The cable and probe show no unsafe physical damage. If damage is found, remove the affected equipment from service and replace or repair it through the approved process.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Accessible Connectors
steps.instructions: Power down as appropriate before manipulating connections. Inspect accessible connector surfaces for: Bent or damaged contacts Debris Moisture Misalignment Loose fit Cracked connector shells Do not force connectors. Expected outcome: Connectors are clean, dry, undamaged, and seat normally. If reseating a loose external connection restores stable communication, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Reseat the Connection
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect the accessible probe or communication connection according to the normal approved connection method. Ensure the connector is fully seated without excessive force. Expected outcome: The probe or connected component is recognized consistently. If communication remains stable after repeated normal movement and use, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 5. Perform a Gentle Movement Check
steps.instructions: With the device off the patient and in a controlled test condition, gently move the cable near: Probe strain relief Connector strain relief Normal bends Docking interface Do not sharply bend, twist, or stress the cable. Expected outcome: Communication remains stable during normal cable movement. If communication drops with gentle movement, remove the device or affected accessory from service and escalate.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Docking Interface
steps.instructions: If the complaint involves docking, inspect accessible docking surfaces and contacts for contamination, damage, improper seating, or mechanical obstruction. Confirm the device sits fully in the dock without rocking or requiring unusual pressure. Expected outcome: Docking is secure and communication remains stable. If cleaning or proper seating corrects the problem, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Use a Known-Good Compatible Accessory When Available
steps.instructions: If facility resources permit, substitute a verified compatible probe, cable, dock, or applicable accessory to isolate the failure. Do not interchange equipment unless compatibility is confirmed. Expected outcome: A known-good component allows stable operation. If substitution identifies a faulty external accessory, replace that accessory and verify normal operation.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Complete a representative scan and confirm: Probe recognition remains stable Communication does not drop during normal positioning Cable movement within normal use does not interrupt operation Docking functions normally when applicable No new warnings or failures occur Expected outcome: Stable operation is verified through a complete representative test. The device may be returned to service.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported the Prime Plus intermittently lost probe communication when the scanner was moved.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external probe connector was not fully seated and communication dropped with normal cable movement.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated the connector, verified stable recognition through repeated movement and representative scanning, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Recognition status before and after reseating
